Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-screenshots.md

# Store screenshots with fastlane

`kinhin mobile init` adds a `screenshots` lane to the iOS and Android projects. It captures localized screenshots from
UI tests (iOS: `snapshot`; Android: `screengrab`), can frame them with frameit, and can upload them to the stores. Upload
is off unless you turn it on. This page covers setup, the folder layout, every setting you can change, and what has been
verified.

[← Back to mobile releases](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-fastlane.md) · [Tutorial](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-fastlane-tutorial.md) · [Troubleshooting](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-fastlane-troubleshooting.md)

Short answers: [How to take App Store screenshots automatically](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-take-app-store-screenshots-automatically.md) · [Run them in CI](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-run-fastlane-screenshots-in-ci-on-a-mac.md) · [Localized screenshots](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-generate-localized-app-store-screenshots.md)

## What you get

| Platform | Capture | Settings file | Where the test lives |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iOS (native, Flutter, React Native) | `snapshot` runs UI tests on simulators | `fastlane/Snapfile`, `fastlane/Framefile.json` | `UITests/` next to the app (see [step 1](#ios-set-up-the-ui-test-target)) |
| Android (native, Flutter, React Native) | `screengrab` runs instrumented tests on an emulator or device | `fastlane/Screengrabfile` | `app/src/androidTest/java/screenshots/` |

`kinhin mobile init` writes the settings, the sample tests and the lane. It does not edit your Xcode project or your Gradle
files, because those are easy to break from a script. The steps that need them are below.

## Run it

```bash
# iOS: from the folder that holds fastlane/ (ios/ for Flutter and React Native)
bundle exec fastlane screenshots

# Android: from the folder that holds fastlane/ (the app root for native; android/ for Flutter and React Native).
# Set the application ID first; the lane builds the two APKs itself.
ANDROID_PACKAGE_NAME=com.example.yourapp bundle exec fastlane screenshots
```

Add `FRAME_SCREENSHOTS=1` to frame the images, or `UPLOAD_SCREENSHOTS=1` to upload them. Both are described below.

The CI workflow runs the same lane when you start it by hand: choose `screenshots` as the lane. The Android job does not run
for the `release` choice, because there is no Android release lane yet.

### Settings from CI

The workflow passes these repository variables (**Settings**, then **Secrets and variables**, then **Variables**) into the
lane. An empty or unset variable means the default. They are variables, not secrets, so do not put anything sensitive in them.

| Variable | Used by | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FRAME_SCREENSHOTS` | iOS | `1` runs frameit (see [Frames](#frames-optional)) |
| `UPLOAD_SCREENSHOTS` | iOS, Android | `1` uploads the screenshots (see [Upload](#upload-optional)) |
| `SNAPSHOT_DEVICES` | iOS | Comma-separated simulator names |
| `SNAPSHOT_LANGUAGES` | iOS | Comma-separated languages (default `en-US`) |
| `SCREENGRAB_LOCALES` | Android | Comma-separated locales (default `en-US`) |
| `SCREENGRAB_DEVICE_TYPE` | Android | `phone`, `sevenInch`, `tenInch`, `tv` or `wear` |

Gitea, Forgejo and GitLab name their variables differently, so check their docs before you rely on these.

### Artifacts

The VM running the job is deleted when the job ends, so the screenshots would disappear with it. The workflow therefore
uploads them as a CI artifact (`ios-screenshots` or `android-screenshots`, kept for 14 days) after the lane, even when the lane
fails. Find the artifact on the workflow run's page. The artifact is visible to everyone who can read the run, so use test
accounts and fake data in the app's screens.

The Android job runs on the same macOS `kinhin-xcode` runner as iOS. screengrab needs an Android emulator or a device on that
runner, which the runner image has to provide. We have not verified that setup on a runner.

## iOS: set up the UI test target

fastlane's snapshot needs a UI test target in the Xcode project. The scaffold writes the test sources; you add the target once.

1. In Xcode, add a **UI Testing Bundle** target (for example `MyAppUITests`) that tests your app.
2. Add `UITests/SnapshotHelper.swift` and `UITests/ScreenshotTests.swift` to that target. The helper is fastlane's
   own file, copied unchanged.
3. Make sure the scheme you use runs the UI tests. Snapshot uses the scheme in `Snapfile`, from `SNAPSHOT_SCHEME` or
   `IOS_SCHEME`. The scheme's Test action must include the UI test target.
4. Keep the test class `@MainActor`. The snapshot helper functions are main-actor isolated, so a test class without it fails
   to build with "Call to main actor-isolated global function 'setupSnapshot'". We hit this with the current Xcode.

Our example does this in XcodeGen. `examples/ios_native_app/project.yml` has the target and the scheme:

```yaml
  IosNativeAppUITests:
    type: bundle.ui-testing
    platform: iOS
    sources: [UITests]
    dependencies:
      - target: IosNativeApp
    settings:
      base:
        GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.iosnativeapp.uitests
        TEST_TARGET_NAME: IosNativeApp
schemes:
  IosNativeApp:
    build:
      targets:
        IosNativeApp: all
        IosNativeAppUITests: [test]
    test:
      targets:
        - IosNativeAppUITests
```

Flutter and React Native apps have a `Runner` or `<App>` project under `ios/` that you open in Xcode. Add the target there the same
way; the Flutter integration-test docs do not cover screenshots, so the native UI test target is the route.

### Customize iOS

`fastlane/Snapfile` reads these, each with a default:

| Setting | Environment variable | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scheme` | `SNAPSHOT_SCHEME`, then `IOS_SCHEME` | none | Must run the UI tests |
| `devices` | `SNAPSHOT_DEVICES` (comma separated) | `iPhone 17e` | Names from `xcrun simctl list devices available`. Without a device list, snapshot can boot several simulators, which is slow |
| `languages` | `SNAPSHOT_LANGUAGES` (comma separated) | `en-US` | One folder per language |
| `output_directory` | edit the file | `./fastlane/screenshots` | Read against the project folder |
| `clear_previous_screenshots` | edit the file | `true` | A deleted screen does not stay in the upload |
| `stop_after_first_error` | edit the file | `false` | |

Empty values from CI are treated as unset. Add `testplan`, `only_testing` or any other snapshot option to the file as you
need. The fastlane page lists them all.

### iOS output

A run writes one PNG per `snapshot("name")` call and language, named after the device:

```
fastlane/screenshots/
  en-US/
    iPhone 17e-01-home.png
  screenshots.html
```

We verified this layout by running the lane on an iPhone 17e simulator. The lane checks that at least one PNG exists, because
snapshot can exit 0 when the tests fail to build or run. The lane then stops with a message instead of passing silently.

## React Native iOS: set up

The React Native iOS example needs three things beyond the UI test target:

- **Build the JavaScript into the Debug app.** The Debug simulator build skips bundling, so run the lane with
  `FORCE_BUNDLING=1 bundle exec fastlane screenshots`. Without it the app shows a red "No script URL" screen.
- **Adopt the iOS 27 scene lifecycle.** Add `UIApplicationSceneManifest` to `Info.plist` and create the window in a
  `SceneDelegate`. Without it the UI test crashes with SIGTRAP.
- **Pass the language to the app.** `SnapshotHelper` sets `-AppleLanguages`, but React Native's `Settings.get('AppleLanguages')`
  does not return it. The UI test passes its own launch argument, and the app reads it:

  ```swift
  app.launchArguments += ["-KinhinLanguage", Snapshot.deviceLanguage]
  ```

  ```ts
  const launched = Settings.get('KinhinLanguage') as string | undefined;
  ```

The example `examples/RnApp` does all three. Use a Release build for store screenshots, since the Debug build shows a
warning banner.

## Android: set up the instrumented tests

screengrab needs these in the Android project, once:

1. **Gradle dependencies** in `app/build.gradle.kts`, with `testInstrumentationRunner` set. Versions are the current releases
   on Google's and Maven Central's repositories:

   ```kotlin
   android {
       defaultConfig {
           testInstrumentationRunner = "androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner"
       }
   }

   dependencies {
       androidTestImplementation("androidx.test:runner:1.7.0")
       androidTestImplementation("androidx.test.ext:junit:1.3.0")
       androidTestImplementation("junit:junit:4.13.2")
       androidTestImplementation("tools.fastlane:screengrab:2.1.1")
   }
   ```

2. **`android.useAndroidX=true`** in `gradle.properties`. The AndroidX test libraries fail to build without it.
3. **Debug permissions.** `app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml` must declare the five permissions screengrab needs. The scaffold
   writes them. If that file already exists (Flutter always has one, with `INTERNET`), the scaffold keeps it and prints a note;
   merge the permissions in by hand:

   ```xml
   <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.DISABLE_KEYGUARD" />
   <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WAKE_LOCK" />
   <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" />
   <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" />
   <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CHANGE_CONFIGURATION" />
   ```

The sample test is `app/src/androidTest/java/screenshots/ScreenshotTest.java`. It launches the app's launcher activity, waits
for the first frame, and calls `Screengrab.screenshot("01-home")`. The `LocaleTestRule` class rule switches the locale for each
entry in `Screengrabfile`. Add a test method per screen.

The example `examples/android_native_app` has all of this. `./gradlew assembleDebugAndroidTest` compiles it, and the e2e checks
that.

### Customize Android

`fastlane/Screengrabfile` reads these:

| Setting | Environment variable | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_package_name` | `ANDROID_PACKAGE_NAME` | none, so it must be set | The `applicationId` of the app under test. Without it screengrab stops with `No value found for 'app_package_name'` |
| `locales` | `SCREENGRAB_LOCALES` (comma separated) | `en-US` | One folder per locale |
| `device_type` | `SCREENGRAB_DEVICE_TYPE` | `phone` | `phone`, `sevenInch`, `tenInch`, `tv` or `wear` |
| `output_directory` | edit the file | `./fastlane/metadata/android` | Google Play's metadata layout |
| `clear_previous_screenshots` | edit the file | `true` | |
| `app_apk_path`, `tests_apk_path` | edit the file | `app/build/outputs/apk/...` | The APKs the lane builds with Gradle. screengrab does not build them |

The screenshots lane runs `assemble` and `assembleDebugAndroidTest` before screengrab. Without the two APK paths screengrab
asks for them in a prompt, which fails in CI.

### Android output

A run of `fastlane screenshots` with `en-US` and the default device type writes:

```
fastlane/metadata/android/
  en-US/images/phoneScreenshots/01-home_<timestamp>.png
  screenshots.html
```

screengrab appends a timestamp to each file name, so `Screengrab.screenshot("01-home")` writes `01-home_<timestamp>.png`.
`screenshots.html` is a report that screengrab writes next to the locale folders; it is not an upload file. Both are
ignored by `examples/.gitignore`.

## Locales

Set the list of languages and the lane captures each one, in its own folder:

```bash
SNAPSHOT_LANGUAGES=en-US,fr-FR bundle exec fastlane screenshots   # iOS
SCREENGRAB_LOCALES=en-US,fr-FR bundle exec fastlane screenshots   # Android
```

Your app has to show different text for each language. On iOS that means a String Catalog (`Localizable.xcstrings`) with
a translation for each language; on Android, `values-fr/strings.xml` next to `values/strings.xml`. Otherwise every locale
folder holds the same English screen. The examples show the pattern: `examples/ios_native_app/App/Localizable.xcstrings`
and `examples/android_native_app/app/src/main/res/values-fr/strings.xml`.

## Frames (optional)

Set `FRAME_SCREENSHOTS=1` and the lane runs frameit on the screenshots folder. Settings go in `fastlane/Framefile.json`. The
scaffold writes valid JSON: a black frame, 50-pixel padding, and no entries under `data`.

**Status: frames are implemented but not yet working on Homebrew's ImageMagick 7.1.2-33.** frameit calls
`magick mogrify -rotate 0 <file>` with no output format, and that build fails with "no encode delegate for this image format
`'". The same operation with `-format png` succeeds. Upstream reports it as
[ImageMagick issue #9011](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/9011), with a fix committed on October 11, 2026.
Until a Homebrew release includes that fix, frames will stop with an error. The lane checks whether frameit changed any
screenshot, because frameit can exit 0 without framing anything.

Things to know:

- **ImageMagick is installed for you.** When frames are on and no `magick` or `convert` command is available, the lane runs
  `brew install imagemagick`. It stops with a clear message if Homebrew is missing, since installing Homebrew needs an admin
  password. Frames also need the first-run download of the device frames.
- **Framed images without titles keep the full device resolution**, and the frameit docs say App Store Connect cannot take
  them. The lane therefore refuses to upload framed images unless you set `ALLOW_FRAMED_UPLOAD=1`, which you should do only once
  `Framefile.json` has titles.

## Upload (optional)

Set `UPLOAD_SCREENSHOTS=1` to upload. Upload is off by default, and the release lanes keep their existing skip settings.

- **iOS** uses `upload_to_app_store` with `skip_binary_upload`, `skip_metadata` and `skip_app_version_update`, and reads
  `./fastlane/screenshots`. `overwrite_screenshots` is set to true; see the deliver docs for its exact behaviour.
- **Android** uses `upload_to_play_store` with the APK and AAB and metadata uploads skipped, and reads
  `./fastlane/metadata/android`. It needs `PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`.

The upload settings are checked against fastlane 2.241.0 by the e2e. Nothing in this repository calls the stores; you run the
upload yourself, with your own credentials. See [credentials](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-credentials.md).

## Other frameworks

- **Capacitor and Ionic:** the screenshot files are scaffolded under `ios/UITests/` and `android/app/src/androidTest/`, but the
  Xcode UI test target (`App`'s UI tests in `ios/App/App.xcodeproj`) and the Gradle test dependencies are added by hand, as
  for React Native and Flutter.
- **Kotlin Multiplatform:** the UI test target goes in `iosApp/` (`iosApp/UITests/`), and the instrumented tests go in
  `androidApp/src/androidTest/`. The Android module is `androidApp`, not `app`, so the paths have no `app/` prefix.
- **.NET MAUI:** no screenshot files. MAUI does not generate UI test projects, so this stays out of the scaffold.

## In a launch video

The screenshots can feed a launch cut. `examples/mobile-30s` shows them with a locale beat, and `video.yml` captures them in a
`mobile-capture` job for a look that sets `screens`. See [CI video](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/ci-video.md#store-screenshots-in-the-mobile-cut) and
[making a video](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/making-a-video.md#screenshots-as-a-scene).

## What is verified

- **iOS capture:** `fastlane screenshots` ran the UI test on an iPhone 17e simulator, wrote `fastlane/screenshots/en-US/iPhone 17e-01-home.png`,
  and the image shows the app's first screen. The lane exits 0 only when at least one PNG exists.
- **iOS build:** the UI test target compiles with the `@MainActor` requirement.
- **Android capture:** `fastlane screenshots` ran on a Pixel 9 emulator (Android 37, arm64) and wrote
  `fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/phoneScreenshots/01-home_<timestamp>.png` at 1080 x 2424. The lane exits 0 only when at least one PNG exists.
- **Locales:** both platforms captured `en-US` and `fr-FR` in one run, each in its own folder, and the French images show French text.
  iOS wrote `fastlane/screenshots/fr-FR/iPhone 17e-01-home.png`; Android wrote `fastlane/metadata/android/fr-FR/images/phoneScreenshots/`.
  The sample apps in `examples/` translate their one string, so the locale switch is visible in the image.
- **Flutter iOS capture:** `fastlane screenshots` ran on iPhone 17e and wrote `en-US` and `fr-FR` 1170 x 2532 PNGs. Each shows the greeting in its language.
- **React Native iOS capture:** `fastlane screenshots` ran on iPhone 17e and wrote `en-US` and `fr-FR` 1170 x 2532 PNGs. Each shows the greeting in its language. The Debug build needs `FORCE_BUNDLING=1` (see [React Native iOS](#react-native-ios-set-up)).
  The French image was taken before the sample showed French text, so it does not prove the locale switch.
- **Flutter and React Native Android capture:** both locales show the greeting in the right language, on a Pixel 9 emulator, for
  both examples. The React Native lane needs Metro running and `adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081` (the Debug build loads its
  JavaScript from Metro). The React Native debug manifest declares the Bluetooth permissions the sample asks for.
- **Android build:** `assembleDebugAndroidTest` compiles the instrumented test with the dependencies above.
- **Options:** every snapshot, screengrab, frameit and screenshot-upload option the templates use exists in fastlane 2.241.0.
- **frameit prerequisite:** frameit stops without ImageMagick. The lane installs it when frames are on.

## What is not verified

- **Frames** end to end. Blocked by [ImageMagick #9011](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/9011) until a release contains the fix.
  The framed output's file name is also unknown.
- **Multiple devices** on iOS. The iOS runs used one simulator (iPhone 17e); the layout for several devices is from the snapshot docs.
- **Debug banner.** React Native Debug builds show an "Open debugger to view warnings" banner in the screenshots. Use a Release build for store screenshots.
- **`simctl diagnose` can hang after a React Native test.** xcodebuild starts it after each test. Kill it and the lane continues.
- **Flutter iOS debug simulator build.** `flutter build ios --simulator --debug` fails on this toolchain (see
  [troubleshooting](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-fastlane-troubleshooting.md#screenshots)); the example builds with `xcodebuild` and `ARCHS=arm64`.
- **Uploads** against real stores. Not run, by decision.

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-fastlane-troubleshooting.md

# Mobile releases: troubleshooting

The failures we have hit while building and testing the integration, with the cause and the fix. Each heading is the
text of the error, so search for it.

[← Back to mobile releases](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-fastlane.md) · [Tutorial](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-fastlane-tutorial.md) · [Credentials](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-credentials.md)

## Setup and scaffolding

### `no iOS or Android project in ...; pass --framework`

`kinhin mobile init` found neither an `ios/` nor an `android/` folder, nor an Xcode project or Gradle settings file, and no
`pubspec.yaml` or `expo`/`react-native` entry in `package.json`. Run it in the project folder, or pass `--framework`.

### `no ios/ or android/ folder in ... for a flutter project`

A Flutter or React Native project needs its native folders. Create them with `flutter create .` or
`npx react-native init`, or generate them for Expo with `npx expo prebuild`, then run `kinhin mobile init` again.

### `Gemfile exists but cannot be read`

The project's `Gemfile` exists but is not readable by your user. Fix its permissions and run the command again.

### `bundler could not find compatible versions for gem "ruby"`

fastlane 2.241, which the `~> 2.240` pin resolves to, needs Ruby 3.2 or newer. The macOS system Ruby is 2.6, so `bundle install` fails with that message. Use
Ruby 3.3, for example from Homebrew (`brew install ruby@3.3`), and run `bundle install` from a shell where that Ruby is first
on your PATH. CI installs Homebrew's Ruby on the runner (`brew install ruby`), so no Actions marketplace action is needed.

### Expo: the EAS config is there, but there is no `fastlane` folder

That is expected. Expo uses EAS Build and EAS Submit by default, and `kinhin mobile init` writes `eas.json` only. For
fastlane, run `npx expo prebuild`, then `kinhin mobile init --framework react-native`. The reference page has the details.

## Local builds

### `deployment target ... is set to 13.0`

Xcode 26 needs an iOS deployment target of 15.0 or higher. `flutter create` still writes 13.0, and `kinhin mobile init` prints a note naming the file when it finds a lower value. Change
`IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` in `ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` to 15.0 (and the `platform :ios` line in the
Podfile, if there is one).

### `Binary ... does not contain architectures "arm64 x86_64"` (Flutter, simulator)

The Flutter Debug simulator build does not work with the Flutter version we tested (3.41): `Flutter.framework` has no
simulator architectures, with or without `--config-only`, or `flutter build ios --simulator --debug`. The release lane
does not use the simulator. Check the iOS side with the Release device build, which is what the lane's archive step runs:
`xcodebuild -workspace Runner.xcworkspace -scheme Runner -sdk iphoneos -configuration Release build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`
after `flutter build ios --config-only --release`. The CI workflow does exactly that.

### `No release AAB at app/build/outputs/bundle/...`

Gradle did not produce the bundle where the lane looks. Check the Gradle output in the log. For Flutter the bundle is under
`build/app/outputs/bundle/release/`, which the lane finds automatically. If another step built the bundle, set `AAB_PATH` to
its location.

### `Keystore not found at ...`

`ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PATH` points to a file that does not exist. In CI the workflow writes the keystore from
`ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64` during the job. If that step did not run, check that the secret is set and that its base64 decodes
(`base64 --decode` on the value).

### `Could not find a Podfile` or `No Podfile found`

The project has no Podfile. Flutter projects without plugins that need CocoaPods, and native projects without CocoaPods, do
not have one. The CI job runs `pod install` only when a Podfile exists, so this is not an error in the workflow.

## Repository and Xcode

### The Flutter or React Native Xcode project is missing in a clean clone

The `.gitignore` of a repository that contains `*.xcodeproj` excludes Xcode projects. Generated projects must be tracked
explicitly. Remove the rule for your project's `ios/` folder, or force-add `project.pbxproj` and the shared schemes. Do not
commit `xcuserdata/`.

### `Could not automatically select an Xcode project` (CocoaPods)

`pod install` could not find an `.xcodeproj` in `ios/`. Check the project is there and tracked by git.

## Secrets and CI

### `Missing environment variables: ...`

The lane stops before any store call and names the variables it needs. Set the secrets listed in
`.github/workflows/mobile-release.yml`. The [credentials](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-credentials.md) page explains each one.

### `ASC_KEY_FILEPATH does not exist: ...`

The `.p8` file was not written. Check the **Write App Store Connect API key** step of the job, and that `ASC_KEY_P8` is
the full contents of the file, including the BEGIN and END lines.

### `Could not find any matching profile` or match fails on CI

`match` runs readonly on CI, so it cannot create missing certificates. Run `MATCH_READONLY=false bundle exec fastlane match appstore`
once from a trusted machine to create them. Check that `MATCH_GIT_URL` is readable from the runner, and that
`MATCH_PASSWORD` is the passphrase the repository was encrypted with.

### `Keychain` or signing errors on the runner

The iOS lanes call `setup_ci` on CI, which makes a temporary keychain. If the runner's keychain is locked or has no access to the
signing identity, the build fails with a codesign error. Check the job log for the keychain step, and that the runner is a
macOS machine with Xcode.

### `Upload fails with 403` (Google Play)

The service account lacks the permission for this app. Grant it **Release apps to testing tracks** in Play Console under
**Users and permissions**. A brand-new app may also need its first release uploaded by hand.

### `The bundle is unsigned` or `jar is unsigned`

The release bundle was built without the upload keystore. The lane passes the keystore to Gradle as
`android.injected.signing.*`. Check the four `ANDROID_KEY*` and `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_*` secrets, and the log of the Gradle step.

## Screenshots

### `snapshot wrote no screenshots`, or `screengrab wrote no screenshots`

snapshot and screengrab can exit 0 when the UI or instrumented tests do not build or run, so the lane checks that a PNG exists.
Check the UI test target (iOS) or the instrumented tests (Android), the scheme in `Snapfile` (`SNAPSHOT_SCHEME`, falling back to
`IOS_SCHEME`), and the test log printed above the message. The [screenshots guide](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-screenshots.md#ios-set-up-the-ui-test-target)
covers the setup.

### `frameit changed no screenshots`

frameit exited without framing anything. On Homebrew's ImageMagick 7.1.2-33, frameit's rotate step fails with
`mogrify: no encode delegate for this image format '`. Upstream bug:
[ImageMagick #9011](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/9011). Frames work again once a Homebrew release contains
the fix; until then, leave `FRAME_SCREENSHOTS` unset.

### `frameit needs ImageMagick, and Homebrew is not installed`

With `FRAME_SCREENSHOTS=1` the lane installs ImageMagick with `brew install imagemagick` when no `magick` or `convert` command is
found. Homebrew itself needs an admin password, so the lane stops instead. Install Homebrew from [brew.sh](https://brew.sh), or
install ImageMagick yourself.

### `Framed screenshots can be rejected by App Store Connect without titles`

`UPLOAD_SCREENSHOTS=1` with frames on would upload framed images at full device resolution, which the frameit docs say App Store
Connect cannot take. Add titles in `Framefile.json`, then set `ALLOW_FRAMED_UPLOAD=1`, or turn frames off.

### `flutter build ios --simulator --debug` fails with a `lipo` error

Flutter 3.41 runs `lipo -verify_arch arm64 x86_64` in one call, which Xcode 26's `lipo` rejects ("requires exactly one input
file"). Build the simulator app with `xcodebuild -workspace Runner.xcworkspace -scheme Runner -sdk iphonesimulator ARCHS=arm64
ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=YES build`, then run the lane. `flutter build ios --simulator --profile` is not supported.

### The UI test crashes with SIGTRAP on iOS 27

UIKit requires the app to adopt the scene lifecycle. Add `UIApplicationSceneManifest` to `Info.plist` and create the window in
a `SceneDelegate`; the React Native example does this.

### Android screenshots are blank, or a permission prompt covers the app

The app may not have drawn yet when screengrab captures, or the app asks for a permission (React Native asks for Bluetooth).
Grant the permission before the lane, or wait for the first frame in the instrumented test.

### `app_package_name` is missing

Set `ANDROID_PACKAGE_NAME` in the environment. A shell variable that is not exported does not reach fastlane.

## Capacitor, Kotlin Multiplatform and .NET MAUI

### `invalid source release: 21` when building a Capacitor Android app

Capacitor 8's Android library compiles with Java 21. Run Gradle with a JDK 21 (`JAVA_HOME`). The CI job uses Java 21 for
Capacitor projects. The other frameworks use Java 17.

### Capacitor iOS build: `App.xcodeproj does not exist`

The Xcode project is in `ios/App/`, one folder below the fastlane folder. Set `IOS_PROJECT=App/App.xcodeproj` for a local
run. The CI job sets it. If the project is missing from a clone, check the `.gitignore` exception: the repository ignores
`*.xcodeproj` unless a rule re-includes it (the `examples/capacitor_app` rule shows the form).

### Kotlin Multiplatform: `Unsupported class file major version 70` or `IllegalArgumentException: 26`

Gradle or Kotlin is running on JDK 26. Use JDK 17 (or 21 for newer Gradle). Export `JAVA_HOME` before a plain `./gradlew` run.

### Kotlin Multiplatform: `embedAndSignAppleFrameworkForXcode` fails when run by hand

The task reads the variables Xcode sets (`SRCROOT`, `CONFIGURATION`, `SDK_NAME`, `ARCHS`). Build through `xcodebuild`, which
runs the Xcode build phase, not Gradle directly.

### Kotlin Multiplatform: `No release AAB at .../androidApp/build/outputs/bundle/release/androidApp-release.aab`

The module's bundle is named after the module, not `app`. The lane builds `:androidApp:bundle` when
`ANDROID_GRADLE_MODULE=androidApp` is set. Check that the variable is set and that `ANDROID_GRADLE_DIR=..` points at the
Gradle root.

### .NET MAUI: `CS0118 ... MauiApp` (ambiguous with `Microsoft.Maui.Hosting.MauiApp`)

A project named `MauiApp` collides with the MAUI hosting type. Rename the project, or qualify the type as
`Microsoft.Maui.Hosting.MauiApp` in the files that use it.

### .NET MAUI: `dotnet publish wrote no IPA` or signing errors on the iOS lane

The publish needs the signing identity and profile that `match` installed. Set `MAUI_CODESIGN_KEY` and
`MAUI_PROVISIONING_PROFILE` (see [.NET MAUI signing](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-credentials.md#net-maui-signing)). The iOS build runs on macOS
only, and needs the .NET 10 SDK with the MAUI workload.

## Verification

If something fails that is not listed here, run the same steps locally with `kinhin mobile init --dry-run` and the lanes, and
compare with the examples in the repository. The `examples/` folder holds a working project for each framework.

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/hardware.md

# Hardware requirements & sizing

What your Mac needs to run kinhin, and how to size CPU, memory, and storage for the fleet you want.

[← Back to README](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/index.md)

kinhin runs a whole VM (or container) per job, so "how big a Mac do I need" really means "how many concurrent jobs do I
want". The scaler never spawns more than the host can hold, and `kinhin doctor` tells you what that is.

## Minimum requirements

| Component  | Minimum                       | Notes                                                                     |
| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chip       | Apple Silicon (any M-series)  | arm64 only; Intel Macs are not supported                                  |
| macOS      | 15 or newer                   | Same as the [install requirements](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md)                            |
| Memory     | 16 GB                         | 8 GB Macs: Linux containers or a single small [Tart Linux VM](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/runtimes.md#tart-linux-vms) |
| Free disk  | ~60 GB                        | The prepared base image plus one VM's scratch                             |
| CPU        | Any Apple Silicon (≥ 8 cores) | The default 4-vCPU VM fits beside the `reserve.cpu: 2` headroom           |
| Hypervisor | [Tart](https://tart.run)      | macOS jobs always need it; Linux jobs use apple/container, Docker, or a Tart Linux VM |

The disk minimum covers one VM: the prepared base image takes roughly 40–60 GB (Xcode-baked
images are larger), and each runner VM is a linked clone of it that grows as the job writes.

## What actually limits concurrency

The scaler computes a cap from the host (see [How scaling works](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/scaling.md#capacity)):

```
cap = min(max_runners,
          (cores − reserve.cpu) / vm.cpu,
          (RAM − reserve.memory_gb) / vm.memory_gb,
          free_disk / disk_per_vm)
```

Three things to know before you size anything:

- **The formula is the contract.** The engine never overcommits CPU, RAM, or disk — a burst past
  the cap queues instead of thrashing your Mac.
- **macOS guests cap at two.** Apple's Virtualization framework and license allow two concurrent
  macOS VMs, whatever the hardware (see [Why kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md#why-the-usual-workarounds-fall-short);
  Linux guests and containers are not subject to it). Beyond two concurrent macOS jobs the knob is
  `runners_per_vm` — several runner processes share one VM, so size `vm.cpu`/`vm.memory_gb` for
  the _sum_ of those jobs.
- **`kinhin doctor` is the source of truth.** It prints your cores, RAM, free disk, the computed
  cap, and which constraint binds.

## CPU (`vm.cpu`)

A vCPU is a share of the host's logical cores (performance and efficiency alike; the scheduler
decides where work lands). What matters is the sum across VMs staying within `cores − reserve.cpu`:

| Workload                                      | `vm.cpu`            |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| Lint, unit tests, small Node/Go/Python builds | 2                   |
| General-purpose (kinhin's default)            | 4                   |
| Xcode, Rust, C++ — compile-heavy              | 4–6                 |
| Shared VM with `runners_per_vm: 2–3`          | 4–8 (cover the sum) |

- Keep `reserve.cpu` at the default 2 if you work on the Mac while CI runs; 4 on an 8-core base
  chip keeps interactive work snappy, and near 0 only makes sense on a dedicated builder.

## Memory (`vm.memory_gb`)

Memory is the constraint that binds first on most Macs, and the one that makes the machine
unusable if you guess low:

| Workload                                     | `vm.memory_gb`       |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| Lint, unit tests, small services             | 4                    |
| General-purpose (kinhin's default)           | 8                    |
| Xcode small–medium app                       | 8–12                 |
| Xcode large app + simulator runs             | 12–16                |
| Flutter/Android on macOS (Java + Android SDK)| 8–12                 |
| Shared VM with `runners_per_vm: n`           | the sum of the jobs  |

- Keep `reserve.memory_gb` at the default 4 or more if the Mac is also your daily driver: the
  scaler reserves that RAM on paper, but macOS still swaps when everything wants memory at once.
- 8 GB Macs have no headroom for a useful macOS VM (8 − 4 reserve = 4 GB): use Linux — containers
  or a single small [Tart Linux VM](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/runtimes.md#tart-linux-vms) — or, for repositories you fully
  trust, [host mode](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/runtimes.md#host-mode-run-jobs-directly-on-your-mac).

## Watching real usage

The figures above are configured capacity; kinhin also shows what is actually used. The menu bar, Fleet tab and
`kinhin status` show host CPU and RAM and per-VM usage (see
[Live CPU and RAM usage](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/v0.0.1-beta-4/docs/app.md#live-cpu-and-ram-usage)). Host RAM used is active + wired + compressed memory, the same
as **Memory Used** in Activity Monitor, against the Mac's total. A VM's RAM is shown against its configured
`vm.memory_gb`, so a VM sitting near its limit is a sign to raise it, and a host near its total is a sign to lower
concurrency or `vm.memory_gb`. VM CPU is a percentage of one core: 400% means about four vCPUs
busy. It is a live reading only, with no history.

## Storage

What kinhin puts on disk, and how much to plan for:

| Item                                        | Planning number                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Prepared macOS base image                   | ~40–60 GB (Xcode-baked images: more)                                              |
| Per-instance footprint (`disk_per_vm`)      | 50 GB default for Tart VMs (macOS or Linux) and 8 GB for container slots; override with `disk_gb` |
| Download cache (`toolchain_cache.max_gb`)  | 50 GB default, LRU-pruned with 30-day expiry                                      |
| Host reserve (`reserve.disk_gb`)            | 10 GB default; spawns hold below reserve + one instance's footprint               |

Recommendations:

- **60 GB free** runs the minimum fleet — the base image and one small VM. Fine for trying kinhin.
- **120–250 GB free** for a standing two-VM macOS fleet with Xcode work: two 50 GB footprints,
  the base image, and room for the cache to breathe.
- **300 GB+** if you keep several prepared images (macOS + Linux, Xcode variants) and a fat cache
  (Flutter, Android, Playwright browsers). Reclaim anything stale with
  `kinhin cleanup [--image] [--cache]`.
- Keep `reserve.disk_gb` at 10 or more, and ~10 % of the SSD free overall — APFS degrades when the
  disk is nearly full. The scaler already holds spawns before the reserve is eaten; cache growth
  is bounded separately by [auto-pruning](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/toolchains.md#expiry-and-pruning).

## Recommended setups

What fits, by Mac memory (with the default `reserve.cpu: 2`, `reserve.memory_gb: 4`):

| Mac      | macOS fleet                                                       | Linux-only alternative     |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| 8 GB     | Not recommended                                                   | 2 slots × (2 cpu / 2 GB)   |
| 16 GB    | 1–2 × (3–4 cpu / 6 GB); two VMs only on 10-core chips             | 3 slots × (2 cpu / 4 GB)   |
| 24 GB    | 2 × (4 cpu / 8 GB)                                                | 4–5 slots × (2 cpu / 4 GB) |
| 32 GB    | 2 × (4–6 cpu / 10–12 GB)                                          | 5–7 slots × (2 cpu / 4 GB) |
| 48–64 GB | 2 × (6–7 cpu / 14–16 GB), `runners_per_vm: 2` → 4 concurrent jobs | 6–8 slots × (2 cpu / 4 GB) |

The macOS shapes assume a 10-core chip or better (two 4-vCPU VMs plus `reserve.cpu: 2` need 10 logical cores). On an
8-core chip, use one VM or smaller shapes. Two macOS VMs is the ceiling on every row; more concurrent macOS jobs come
from `runners_per_vm`.

Example: a 16 GB Mac mini (M4, 10 cores) running Linux CI in apple/container microVMs.

```yaml
max_runners: 3
runtimes:
  default: appleContainer
container:
  image: "kinhin-ci-linux"
  cpus: 2
  memory_gb: 4
```

The cap is (10 − 2) / 2 = 4 by CPU and (16 − 4) / 4 = 3 by RAM, so three concurrent jobs.

## Sizing in practice

1. Pick a workload row from the CPU and memory tables above; set `vm.cpu` / `vm.memory_gb`.
2. Set `max_runners` to the concurrency you want — the real cap is the smaller of that and what
   the host can hold.
3. Run `kinhin doctor` and read the binding constraint; adjust the shape or the `reserve:` until
   the cap matches your intent.
4. Watch one real burst with `kinhin watch`: jobs queuing mean too few VMs (or a too-tight cap);
   jobs timing out mean the VMs are too small.

Serving one repo from several Macs splits the load, and each Mac still sizes itself independently
([Running on multiple Macs](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/scaling.md#running-on-multiple-macs)).

No spare Mac? See [Running kinhin on a rented Mac](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/rented-mac.md).

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/rented-mac.md

# Running kinhin on a rented Mac

Run a kinhin fleet on a Mac you rent by the month instead of one on your desk: a colocated Mac mini
or a bare-metal cloud Mac. This is also how a team or consultancy can run CI for someone else: one
dedicated Mac per customer, their own forge token, no shared hardware.

[← Back to README](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/index.md)

kinhin is a single-owner tool: one Mac, one set of forge tokens, one operator. Renting a Mac does
not change that. You get a machine without having to own or host one, and everything else on this
page is the normal [install and setup](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md) with a few remote-specific steps.

## Choosing a host

Any provider that gives you a dedicated Apple Silicon Mac with a GUI login session works. Compare
current prices and terms on each provider's own page; they change often.

| Option                   | Billing shape                  | Notes                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mac mini colocation/rent | Monthly                        | Cheapest per month for a standing fleet (for example MacStadium)      |
| Apple Silicon bare metal | Monthly or hourly, by provider | Check the provider's minimum lease; Apple's license sets one for hosted Macs |
| AWS EC2 Mac              | Per hour, with a 24 h minimum  | Dedicated host; fine for bursts, costly for an always-on fleet        |

Sizing is the same as for a Mac on your desk: see [Hardware requirements & sizing](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/hardware.md).
Remember the macOS ceiling: **two concurrent macOS VMs per Mac**, whatever the hardware. More
macOS concurrency means more Macs (see [running on multiple Macs](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/scaling.md#running-on-multiple-macs))
or `runners_per_vm`.

**Warning: One customer per Mac**

Every job runs in its own VM, but all VMs share one host and, by default, one virtual network (see
[Security](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/security.md)). Do not put two unrelated customers' repositories on the same Mac. If you
resell this setup, give each customer a dedicated Mac and have them create the forge token.
Check the host provider's and Apple's terms on resale and minimum lease periods before you price
anything.
## Bootstrap

SSH in as the Mac's admin user and run the bootstrap script from a checkout of this repository:

```bash
ssh admin@your-mac 'bash -s' < scripts/bootstrap-rented-mac.sh
```

It checks the host (Apple Silicon, macOS 15+, Homebrew), installs Tart and kinhin if they are
missing, creates a starter `config.yaml`, and prints the remaining steps. It is idempotent, and it
never touches a token.

## Configure and authenticate

Edit `~/Library/Application Support/Kinhin/config.yaml`: set the `accounts:` entry for the
customer's forge and the labels their jobs request. Then, in an SSH session on the Mac:

```bash
# Over plain ssh the login Keychain is locked; unlock it for this session
security unlock-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db

kinhin auth set        # prompts for the token; use --gitlab, --gitea, ... for other forges
kinhin doctor          # prerequisites, and how many VMs this Mac can hold
kinhin image prepare   # once; bakes the runner base image
```

Have the customer create a token with the minimum scope their forge needs (see
[Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md)) and type it themselves, or hand it over through a channel you already
trust. Do not put it in a script argument, an environment variable or a shell history.

## Keep it running unattended

`kinhin daemon install` installs a LaunchAgent, which runs in the user's GUI session. On a headless
rented Mac that means:

- Turn on **automatic login** for the admin user (System Settings → Users & Groups), so the session,
  and the login Keychain with it, exists after a reboot. Providers typically document this for their
  machines.
- Keep FileVault off, or you will need to unlock the disk by hand after every reboot. Weigh that
  against the data on the Mac: it holds only a forge token and throwaway VMs.
- If the fleet runs Linux jobs on apple/container or Docker, start those at login as well. See
  [Start at login](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/runtimes.md#start-at-login).
- Install the daemon from that session (a VNC or Screen Sharing login works), then confirm
  with `kinhin status` over SSH.

```bash
kinhin daemon install
kinhin status
```

Finally, dispatch a workflow whose `runs-on` labels match the config and watch it with
`kinhin watch`.

## What this does not give you

- No multi-tenant control plane, remote API or billing. Each Mac is operated like any other kinhin
  host, over SSH.
- No GitHub App authentication yet: kinhin uses a PAT. JIT registration is used only in scale-set mode (see the
  [GitHub notes](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges/github.md)).
- What has run for real is listed in [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md#what-has-been-tested).

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/security.md

# Security

What kinhin protects, what it leaves to you, and the settings to turn on if your jobs can include code you don't fully trust (fork PRs, outside contributors).

[← Back to README](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/index.md)

## The threat model

Every job runs in a fresh VM or container that is deleted afterwards, but VMs run on the same Mac and (for Tart) the same virtual network. The risks that matter are a job reaching another job's VM, your LAN or your Mac; a job reading the credentials its runner registered with; and a job leaving something behind for a later job. Host mode (`runtime: host`) has no isolation at all: use it for repositories you fully trust.

## If you run untrusted PRs: turn these on

Public repository? Start with [Running kinhin for an open-source project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/open-source.md): keeping fork pull
requests off kinhin matters more than any setting below.

| Setting                                    | Why                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tart_softnet: true`                       | Runner VMs reach the internet but not each other or your LAN ([setup](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/runtimes.md#isolating-runner-vms-from-each-other)).                                 |
| `projects[].share_cache: false` (default)   | The shared cache is writable and holds code other jobs execute ([why](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/toolchains.md)).                                                                    |
| Re-run `kinhin image prepare`              | Images baked by older builds still accept the default `admin` SSH password; a fresh prepare turns password login off.                                     |
| No `runtime: host` for those repositories  | Host mode runs jobs directly on your Mac.                                                                                                                 |

## Check your settings with doctor

`kinhin doctor` (and the app's Diagnostics tab) reports the isolation posture: whether `tart_softnet` is on and `softnet` is installed, which accounts send a token over plain http, and which projects have `share_cache` on. Advisories are warnings and never make the report not-ready; the one hard failure is `tart_softnet: true` without `softnet` installed, because the fleet refuses to start in that state. `kinhin doctor --json` carries the same data under `security` (`softnetEnabled`, `softnetInstalled`, `ok`, `fix`, `insecureHTTPAccounts`, `sharedCacheWritable`, `warnings`).

## What kinhin enforces

- **Guest SSH is key-only.** `image prepare` turns off password login in the guest and fails the bake if sshd doesn't honour it.
- **Tokens stay out of reach.** They live in the Keychain (this-device-only), never in `config.yaml`. Registration scripts travel over stdin, so tokens don't appear in `ps` on the host, and the log redactor masks every token format kinhin knows (plus any token it has loaded). `kinhin doctor --bundle` writes a redacted report for bug reports.
- **Forge instances use https.** Gitea, Forgejo and GitLab instances must be `https://` unless the host is loopback or the account sets `allow_insecure_http: true` ([details](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md#plain-http-instances)). Redirects must stay on the same host.
- **Config values can't inject shell.** Toolchain entries are limited to a strict character set and quoted again where they enter a script.
- **The daemon socket and local files are private.** The socket is `0600` in a `0700` directory and only your user can connect. The support directory, logs and state are owner-only.
- **Host mode is repo-scoped.** A config with a `runtime: host` route is refused unless every account is scoped to a single repository (`owner/name`).
- **Updates are verified.** The updater (Sparkle) installs only archives signed with the release's EdDSA key, and a Developer ID build also needs a Gatekeeper-accepted signature; see [Updates and installs](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md#how-updates-and-installs-are-verified).
- **The shared cache is pruned safely.** A symlink planted by a job can't redirect a delete outside the cache.

## Per-project toolchains

A repo's `.kinhin/config.yml` (or the older `.kinhin.yml`) lets repo contents decide what is installed on your Mac, so it is
treated as untrusted input and bounded ([how it works](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/toolchains.md#per-project-toolchains)).

- **Opt-in per repo.** The file is ignored unless a `projects:` entry matching the repo sets
  `repo_file: true` (default `false`).
- **Catalog-only, toolchains-only.** The file may only carry `toolchains.specs` and
  `toolchains.stacks`, and every spec must be a tool in kinhin's curated catalog. There is no
  `brew`, no `provision_script`, no `base_image`, and no cache policy from a repo; free-form mise
  backends are rejected. Values pass the same character allowlist as `config.yaml`, and the file
  is capped at 16 KB.
- **Fork PRs ignore the file.** A pull request from a fork never gets its own `.kinhin/config.yml` (or `.kinhin.yml`)
  honored; the file is read from the base repo's default branch instead. A job whose forge does not
  say whether it is a fork's (GitHub scale-set jobs, Gitea and Forgejo) is treated the same way.
- **`share_cache` exists only per project and is off by default** and forced off for fork PRs and for
  jobs of unknown origin. The cache
  subpath is scoped per project so untrusted repos cannot poison each other's cache.
- **Bad files never block the fleet.** A failed fetch or parse is logged and the job runs on the
  global image.

## The healing agent

The [healing agent](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/healing.md) fixes fleet problems on its own, so its limits are part of the security model.

- **No tokens.** It never stores, reads or replaces a token. A rejected or missing token is shown to you with the
  `kinhin auth set` command, and tokens and setup problems are never offered to the on-device model.
- **A closed list of fixes.** Every fix is one of a fixed set, each running a code path kinhin already has (the same
  prune, install and teardown the CLI uses). Nothing runs a command a model or a log line wrote. Destructive or slow
  fixes (pruning images, installing or rolling back a runtime) wait for your approval, and the MCP server cannot
  approve one.
- **Redacted and owner-only.** Every problem, outcome and advisor explanation passes the log redactor before it is
  stored or shown. The journal (`state/healing.json`, the last 100 entries) is written owner-only.
- **On-device model.** The optional advisor is Apple Intelligence on this Mac (Foundation Models): no account, no
  network call. It sees the redacted problem, the allowed fixes and a few dozen redacted log lines, and kinhin checks its pick
  again before acting.
- **Ollama advisor.** With `healing.ai: ollama`, the same redacted problem and log lines go to the Ollama server named by
  `healing.ollama.host`. On this Mac (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) nothing leaves the machine. Any other host must be
  `https`, and it then receives those lines. Only point `host` at a server you trust with your fleet's logs.
- **Test switches stay out of releases.** `KINHIN_HEALING_TIMINGS` and `KINHIN_HEALING_ADVISOR`, which the e2e suite
  uses to speed the agent up and fix the advisor's answer, are read only by debug builds; release builds never read
  them.

## Telemetry and network calls

kinhin sends no telemetry unless you opt in: the `telemetry:` section is off by default, and when you turn it on it exports only to the OpenTelemetry server you point it at ([Telemetry](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/telemetry.md)). There are no analytics. Otherwise it talks only to the forges you configure (and their runner
download hosts), to kinhin.dev for Sparkle's once-a-day appcast check, and to GitHub Releases for update downloads.
A runtime install you approve in
`kinhin heal` downloads like `kinhin setup repair` does; the healing advisor makes no network calls.

## Known limits

- **Tart guest SSH host-key verification has an unverified fallback.** Before registration, kinhin tries to rotate each guest's SSH host keys through Tart's guest-agent channel, then pins the resulting key and requires strict verification. If the guest agent cannot rotate/read the key before the timeout, or the runtime cannot use the guest-agent channel, kinhin records a warning and continues with host-key checking disabled for that instance. On Tart's default shared network a hostile job in another VM could answer on a booting VM's address and receive its registration material. `tart_softnet: true` isolates runner VMs from each other and the LAN, reducing this risk; enable it when serving untrusted code and investigate any host-key fallback warning. For the warning text kinhin emits and how to separate it from the scale-set registration failures that can follow it, see [Troubleshooting scale sets](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges/github.md#troubleshooting-scale-sets).
- **Registration tokens can be seen by job code in some paths.** With `runners_per_vm > 1` every classic runner is registered before any starts, so the shared registration token is not in `ps` while a job runs. Gitea and host-mode registrations still pass the token as an argument, the Buildkite agent token stays in the agent's environment, and the GitLab runner token file stays on disk until the runner exits. The Azure DevOps PAT is in the guest only while `config.sh` registers the agent. Scope those tokens narrowly.
- **Runners that share an instance can read each other's credentials.** With `runners_per_vm > 1` every runner in an instance runs as the same user, so a job can read a sibling runner's registration (for scale sets, its JIT config: in the runner's command line and the credential files it writes) and take over that runner's later jobs. Use `runners_per_vm: 1` for repositories whose code you do not trust.
- **Docker runners keep Docker's default capabilities** (jobs commonly `apt-get` and `sudo`). kinhin adds a pids limit; for stronger isolation prefer Tart VMs.
- **The toolchain cache is shared, writable and trusted by later jobs** when a project's `share_cache` is on. A job can plant content a later job uses, though each project gets its own cache subdirectory. It defaults to off and is always off for fork PRs and for jobs whose forge does not say whether they come from a fork. Keep it off for untrusted repositories.
- **Any process running as you can control the daemon** over its private socket (stop, token swap). The socket is 0600 in a 0700 directory and checks the peer's uid, not its code signature.
- **The mise installer is not checksum-verified** in Linux image bakes (`mise.run` publishes no digest to pin).

## What stays your responsibility

- Token scopes: give each forge token only what [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md) says it needs.
- `kinhin auth set` hides the token as you type it. Passing `--token` works but warns, because the value lands in shell history and the process list.
- Base images: the curated defaults are `:latest` tags a registry can republish. Pin one with `kinhin image digest` for reproducible bakes.
- A job still runs as the guest's `admin` user with passwordless `sudo`. Isolation comes from the VM boundary, not from restricting the job inside it.

## For maintainers: CI and releases

- CI runs on a self-hosted Mac that also hosts the fleet, so fork PRs are never run there: the `fork` job gives them the
  same lint, tests and release build on a GitHub-hosted Mac. The workflow token is read-only and no workflow uses
  `pull_request_target`.
- The kinhin repository is public, so its org runner group must allow public repositories, limited to this one
  repository; fork workflows need approval for all external contributors.
- Put the signing and notarization secrets in a GitHub **environment** named `release` with required reviewers, and protect `v*` tags, so a pushed tag alone can't reach them.
- Actions are pinned to commit SHAs; bump them deliberately.

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/open-source.md

# Running kinhin for an open-source project

How to use kinhin for a public repository without letting a stranger's pull request run code on your Mac.

[← Back to README](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/index.md) · [Security](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/security.md)

## The risk

A public repository accepts pull requests from anyone. A workflow that runs on a pull request runs the **pull request's
code**: its build scripts, its tests, its changes to the workflow file itself. If that job lands on kinhin, someone you
have never met runs code on your Mac, with internet access, as `admin` with passwordless `sudo` inside the guest.

kinhin's VM boundary is real isolation, and with `vm.ephemeral: true` (the default) every job gets a fresh VM that is
deleted afterwards. But a VM is a
boundary, not a guarantee: the job can use your bandwidth and CPU (mining, spam, attacks on others), probe whatever the
VM can reach, and try to escape. GitHub's own advice is to use self-hosted runners only with private repositories for
exactly this reason ([GitHub: managing access to self-hosted runners][gh-groups]).

The safe pattern is simple: **trusted code runs on kinhin, fork pull requests run on hosted runners.** The rest of this
page is how to set that up, then how to harden kinhin for the code that does reach it.

## 1. Keep fork pull requests off kinhin

Do all three. Each one alone has a gap.

### Keep public repositories out of kinhin's runner group (GitHub)

Organization runners belong to a runner group, and **by default only private repositories can use a runner group**
([GitHub][gh-groups]). Leave it that way unless you need otherwise: under the organization's **Settings → Actions →
Runner groups**, the group kinhin registers into (`scale_set.runner_group`, usually `Default`) should not allow public
repositories. If a public repository must use kinhin, limit the group to **Selected repositories** and list only that
one.

### Route fork pull requests to hosted runners in the workflow

Pick the runner per event, so pushes and your own branches use kinhin and pull requests from forks use a GitHub-hosted
runner:

```yaml
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ${{ (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && 'kinhin' || 'macos-latest' }}
```

Replace `kinhin` with the label or scale-set name your fleet uses (`kinhin-container` for Linux containers, and so on)
and `macos-latest` with the hosted runner you want. `kinhin workflow route` does not edit expressions like this one;
write it by hand.

### Require approval before fork workflows run

In the repository's **Settings → Actions → General**, set **Approval for running fork pull request workflows from
contributors** to **Require approval for all external contributors** ([GitHub][gh-settings]). A maintainer then reads
the pull request and clicks **Approve and run** before anything executes ([approving runs from forks][gh-approve]).
Approve only after reading the diff, including changes to `.github/workflows/`.

### Never check out pull request code under `pull_request_target`

`pull_request_target` runs with the base repository's secrets and a write token. Combined with checking out the pull
request's head, it hands both to the pull request's author, on any runner. Use `pull_request` for anything that builds
or tests the pull request ([GitHub: secure use][gh-secure]).

### GitLab, Gitea and Forgejo

- **GitLab:** merge requests from forks run in the **fork's** project by default, on the fork's runners, so kinhin's
  project runners never see them. Keep it that way: don't run fork pipelines in the parent project unless a maintainer
  has reviewed the change ([merge request pipelines][gl-mr]). kinhin also flags every merge-request pipeline as untrusted.
- **Gitea and Forgejo:** kinhin cannot tell from their APIs whether a job comes from a fork, so it treats every job as
  untrusted (below). Don't register kinhin for a public repository that accepts outside pull requests unless your server
  requires approval for them; check your version's Actions settings.

## 2. Harden kinhin for the code that reaches it

Set these in `config.yaml` for any fleet that serves a public repository, even with fork pull requests routed away:
someone can still open a pull request from a branch of your own repository once they have write access, and
dependencies can be compromised.

```yaml
tart_softnet: true   # runner VMs reach the internet, not each other or your LAN
runners_per_vm: 1    # one job per VM: jobs never share a filesystem
vm:
  ephemeral: true    # a fresh VM per job, deleted afterwards (the default)
projects:
  - pattern: "your-org/public-repo"
    repo_file: false     # the repo cannot choose what is installed (the default)
    share_cache: false   # no writable cache shared between jobs (the default)
```

| Setting | Why |
| ------- | --- |
| `tart_softnet: true` | Without it a job can reach other runner VMs and your local network ([setup](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/runtimes.md#isolating-runner-vms-from-each-other)). |
| `runners_per_vm: 1` | With more than one runner per VM, concurrent jobs share the guest's disk and processes, so one job can tamper with another. |
| `vm.ephemeral: true` | A persistent VM keeps whatever one job left behind for the next. |
| Tart VMs, not Docker or host | Docker containers share one kernel and keep Docker's default capabilities; host mode has no isolation at all. Never add a `host` route for a public repository. |
| `share_cache: false` | The shared toolchain cache is writable and trusted by later jobs. |
| `repo_file: false` | `.kinhin/config.yml` (or `.kinhin.yml`) lets the repository decide which catalog tools are installed. |
| A repository-scoped account | Scope the account to `owner/name`, not the whole organization, so its token can manage only that repository's runners. Give the token only the permissions in [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md). |
| A pinned base image | `kinhin image digest` pins the base so a republished tag cannot change what you bake. |
| A fresh `kinhin image prepare` | Images baked by older builds still allow SSH password login. |

Then run `kinhin doctor`: its security section flags softnet off, plain-http forges and a writable shared cache.

### What kinhin does on its own

- **Runners take one job.** With `vm.ephemeral: true` each job gets a fresh VM or container, deleted when the job ends
  (GitLab accounts require it).
- **Jobs that may come from a fork get no shared cache and no repo file from the pull request,** even if the project
  allows them. kinhin treats a job as possibly a fork's whenever the forge doesn't prove otherwise: GitHub scale-set
  jobs and Gitea and Forgejo jobs always, GitHub workflow runs when the payload lacks the head repository, and GitLab
  merge-request pipelines. Their `.kinhin/config.yml` is read from the default branch instead.
- **Tokens never enter the config,** and the log redacts them.

## 3. Watch it

- `kinhin status` and `kinhin pipeline` show which repository and job each VM is running.
- An unexpected repository in the queue means a runner group or label is wider than you meant.
- Keep `workflow` permissions minimal (`permissions: contents: read` at the top of each workflow), so even an approved
  job gets a read-only token.

## Checklist

- [ ] Runner group excludes public repositories, or lists only the ones you mean.
- [ ] Fork pull requests are routed to hosted runners in the workflow.
- [ ] Approval required for all external contributors.
- [ ] No `pull_request_target` job checks out pull request code.
- [ ] `tart_softnet: true`, `runners_per_vm: 1`, no host route, `share_cache` and `repo_file` off.
- [ ] Repository-scoped account with a narrow token; `kinhin doctor` shows no security warnings.

[gh-groups]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-runners/self-hosted-runners/manage-access
[gh-settings]: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/enabling-features-for-your-repository/managing-github-actions-settings-for-a-repository
[gh-approve]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/approve-runs-from-forks
[gh-secure]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use
[gl-mr]: https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipelines/merge_request_pipelines/

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md

# Add videos to your project

Make a narrated launch video, a feature clip or a README GIF for **your own product**. The video is a config file in your
repository: scenes, a voice-over, music, captions and a theme. One command turns it into an MP4, a WebM, a poster, a GIF
and a caption file. Everything runs in a container, on open-source tools, with no accounts.

[← Back to README](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/index.md) · [Video gallery](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-gallery.md) · [Marketing video in CI](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/ci-video.md)

Short answer: [How to make a product launch video from code](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-make-a-product-launch-video-from-code.md).

## Your first video in 5 minutes

**You need:**

- **kinhin installed** ([Install & updates](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md)).
- **A container runtime**: Apple's `container` (`brew install container && container system start`) or Docker. kinhin uses
  Apple's if it is running, otherwise Docker. `--runtime` picks one.
- **Disk space.** The first build pulls a container image of about 1 GB and needs a few GB free.

No recording is needed for title, statement, stats, steps, code and the other drawn scenes.

**1. Create a starter video** in your repository:

```bash
cd ~/code/acme
kinhin video init launch
```

This writes `.kinhin/videos/launch.yml` and a `.gitignore` for the output. It never overwrites an existing file.

**2. Change the words.** Open `.kinhin/videos/launch.yml`. It has three drawn scenes, each with narration, and comments that
say what each field does. One scene looks like this:

```yaml
  - id: intro
    type: title
    props: { title: Acme, subtitle: Ship faster }
    narration: Acme helps your team ship faster.
```

Each scene has an `id`, a `type`, `props` (what is shown) and `narration` (what is said). The
[scene types](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md#scene-types) are listed in the config reference.

**3. Check it** without rendering anything. It takes seconds once the image is there:

```bash
kinhin video validate launch
```

It lists every problem with its place in the file (an unknown scene type, a clip the adapter does not have, a claim your
`claims.json` forbids). Fix them and run it again, or go straight to the build.

**4. Build it:**

```bash
kinhin video build launch
```

The first run pulls the image. Later builds reuse it and, once it is pulled, need no network.

**5. Find the video** in `.kinhin/videos/out/launch/`: `launch.mp4`, `launch.webm`, `launch-poster.png`, `launch-hero.gif`
and the caption file `launch.srt`. The folder also holds `music-credit.txt` when a music track needs a credit line.

Next steps: [the config reference](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md) (themes, scenes, captions, music), and
[recordings of your product](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-adapters.md) if you want your app or terminal on screen.

## What to commit

| Commit | Ignore (already in the generated `.gitignore`) |
|---|---|
| `.kinhin/videos/*.yml`: your videos | `.kinhin/videos/out/`: the built files |
| `.kinhin/videos/themes/`, `fonts/`, `adapters/` (with `reference/` clips) | `.kinhin/videos/.cache/`: the render cache |
| `.kinhin/videos/music/` (the audio, if you choose to keep it) | |

Commit the music file and its `.json` record together. If you do not commit the audio, anyone who builds the video,
including CI, must run `kinhin video music add` again, or the build stops with a missing file.

## Words used on these pages

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Video** | One config file in `.kinhin/videos/`. It builds to its own folder under `out/`. |
| **Scene** | One part of the video, with its own text and length. Scenes play in order. |
| **Theme** | The look: font, colours, background and the window or laptop frame. Built in or your own. |
| **Narration** | The words the voice-over says for a scene. |
| **Drawn scene** | A scene kinhin draws from its props, such as a title or a list of steps. Needs no recording. |
| **Adapter** | A folder of recordings of your product, used by device and terminal scenes. |
| **Clip** | One recording inside an adapter, such as your app's screen or a terminal session. |

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `kinhin video init [name]` | Writes a starter `.kinhin/videos/<name>.yml` (default `launch`) and a `.gitignore`. Never overwrites. |
| `kinhin video list` | Lists the videos (`--json` for scripts). |
| `kinhin video validate [name]` | Checks a video without rendering it: the same checks the build makes, plus that its clips and music files exist. `--all` checks every video. Exit 3 when one has a problem. |
| `kinhin video build [name]` | Builds one. `--theme`, `--format`, `--captions on\|off\|all`, `--caption-style`, `--music <track\|file\|off>` change the look for one build. `--fast` is a quicker preview with no WebM. `--quality draft\|standard\|high` sets the encode (`draft` is `--fast`; `high` is slower and larger) and `--fps 24\|30\|60` the frame rate (30 by default). `--scene app,outro` builds only those scenes as a quick preview (a draft encode, no music), and `--watch` rebuilds whenever a file under `.kinhin/videos/` changes. |
| `kinhin video music search <words>` | Finds free music. Then `preview`, `add` and `list`; see [Music](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md#music). |
| `kinhin video theme new <name> --from <theme>` | Starts your own theme file; see [Your own theme](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md#your-own-theme). |

### Faster rebuilds

A build keeps what it can reuse in `.kinhin/videos/.cache/` (commit nothing from it; `kinhin video init` ignores it):

| Kept | In | Used again while |
|---|---|---|
| The voice of each sentence | `voice-cache/` | the sentence, the voice and its speed are the same, so a change to one line speaks only that line |
| Title and other drawn scenes | `scenes/` | the scene's props, length, theme and format are the same |
| Framed recordings (laptop, window, split) | `frames/` | the scene's props, length, look and recordings are the same, and so is the framing code; unused ones are cleared after two months |

Every build prints how long each step took. To iterate on one scene, build just that scene, and add `--watch` to rebuild on every save:

```bash
kinhin video build launch --scene app --watch
```

A preview is written to `out/<name>-scene-<ids>/`, so it never replaces the full video. If a rebuild ever shows something old, delete
`.kinhin/videos/.cache/` (or one of its folders from the table) and build again. In a checkout of kinhin, `RENDER_FORCE=1` and `VOICE_FORCE=1`
with `video/scripts/build.sh` frame, render and speak everything again for one build.

`--format` takes `16:9`, `9:16`, `4:5` or `1:1`. Other options: `--dir PATH` (a repository other than the current
directory), `--runtime container|docker`, and `--image REF` (or `KINHIN_VIDEO_IMAGE`) to run a different image.

## Building on a runner or in CI

`kinhin video build` runs on the Mac you type it on. To build somewhere else, add a pipeline file once and commit it:

```bash
kinhin video init --workflow --runs-on self-hosted,linux   # writes .github/workflows/kinhin-video.yml; commit and push it
kinhin video build launch --on-fleet                       # dispatches it, follows the run, downloads the video
```

`--on-fleet` uses the GitHub CLI (`gh`, signed in with `gh auth login`) and works for GitHub repositories. The runner needs
Docker and a network that can reach ghcr.io; nothing in the workflow needs a secret. `--ref BRANCH` runs it on another branch.
The video is downloaded to `.kinhin/videos/out/` as with a local build.

Other CI systems get a pipeline too. `--ci` picks one (by default the repository's own, detected from its CI files and the
host of its `origin` remote), and `--runs-on` sets the runner labels in that system's terms:

| `--ci` | Pipeline file | Default runner | Start it from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gitea`, `forgejo` | `.gitea/workflows/kinhin-video.yml`, `.forgejo/workflows/kinhin-video.yml` | `runs-on: [linux]` | Actions > kinhin video > Run workflow |
| `gitlab` | `.gitlab/kinhin-video.yml`, included from `.gitlab-ci.yml` | `tags: [linux]` | Build > Pipelines > Run pipeline, with `VIDEO_PROJECT` set |
| `bitbucket` | `.kinhin/videos/bitbucket-pipelines.kinhin-video.yml`, to copy into `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` | `self.hosted, linux.shell` | Pipelines > Run pipeline > custom: kinhin-video |
| `azure` | `.azure-pipelines/kinhin-video.yml` | the `kinhin` pool, `demands: [linux]` | a pipeline made from that file |
| `buildkite` | `.buildkite/kinhin-video.yml` | `queue=kinhin` | a pipeline whose steps upload that file |

Each runs the same image with `docker run` and keeps `.kinhin/videos/out` as the `kinhin-video` artifact. `--on-fleet`
starts and downloads the GitHub workflow only: for the other systems, start the pipeline by hand and download the artifact
(running `--on-fleet` there says where to start it).

kinhin's own repository also builds its videos in GitHub Actions on a release or a pull request, opt-in and with no secrets:
see [Marketing video in CI](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/ci-video.md).

## In the app

The menu bar app has the same thing in a window: on the Fleet tab, **Make a Video…** lets you choose a repository, create or pick
a video in its `.kinhin/videos/`, build it (with a fast-preview option and live output, then **Show in Finder**), and search free
music and add a track to the selected video. It runs the same code as `kinhin video`, so the runtime, the image and every file are
the same.

## Examples

The kinhin repository's [`video/script/examples/`](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/tree/main/video/script/examples) has a dozen
finished videos. Copy one into `.kinhin/videos/` to start from it. Each uses a different theme, format, voice and mix of scenes:
`hello` (the smallest), `scene-tour` (every drawn scene type), `social-teaser` (9:16), `tutorial-chalk`, `code-walkthrough`
and others. [The gallery](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-gallery.md) shows each one. `kinhin-30s` uses kinhin's own adapter, which is built into the image,
so it is a worked example rather than a template for your product.

| Page | Read it for |
|---|---|
| [Config reference](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md) | The project file, themes, scene types, captions, music, voices |
| [Recordings of your product](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-adapters.md) | Adapters, clips, recording your app or terminal, the claims check |
