# Video config reference

Everything a video file can say. Start with the [first video](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md#your-first-video-in-5-minutes) if you
have not built one yet. Each video is one YAML or JSON file in `.kinhin/videos/`; the fields below go at its top level.

[← Back to Add videos to your project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md) · [Recordings](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-adapters.md) · [Troubleshooting](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-troubleshooting.md)

**On this page:** [The project file](#the-project-file) · [Your own theme](#your-own-theme) · [Scene types](#scene-types) ·
[Camera](#camera-on-recordings) · [Speed ramps](#speed-ramps) · [Split screen](#split-screen) · [Transitions](#transitions) · [Captions](#captions) · [Music](#music) · [Build flags](#build-flags)

## The project file

```json
{
  "name": "My product",
  "theme": "midnight",
  "format": "16:9",
  "pace": 1,
  "voice": { "engine": "kokoro", "name": "af_heart" },
  "overrides": { "font": { "family": "Georgia" }, "colors": { "accent": "#ff7a59" } },
  "scenes": [
    { "id": "intro", "type": "title", "props": { "title": "Hello", "subtitle": "my product" },
      "narration": "Meet my product." }
  ]
}
```

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `name` | The video's title, shown in `kinhin video list`. |
| `theme` | One of the built-in themes, or one of yours ([below](#your-own-theme)). |
| `format` | `16:9` (default), `9:16` (vertical), `4:5` or `1:1`. |
| `pace` | `0.7` (slower) to `1.6` (faster). Scales the voice and the pauses. |
| `voice` | The narrator. See [Voices](#voices). |
| `overrides` | Changes to the theme for this video only, merged over the theme: `{font: {family: Georgia}, colors: {accent: "#ff7a59"}}`. |
| `adapter` | The product whose recordings the scenes use, by name. Optional for videos made only of drawn scenes. See [Recordings](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-adapters.md). |
| `transition` | How scenes hand over to each other: `fade` (default), `dissolve`, `push`, `slide`, `wipe` or `circle`. A scene can set its own. See [Transitions](#transitions). |
| `captions`, `music` | See [Captions](#captions) and [Music](#music). |
| `scenes` | The scenes, in order. See [Scene types](#scene-types). |

### Voices

`voice: { engine: kokoro, name: af_heart }`. Builds run in the container, which includes **`kokoro`** only (Apache-2.0 model).
Its voices include `af_heart` (default), `af_bella`, `am_michael`, `bf_emma` and `bm_george`. The `supertonic` and macOS `say`
engines need tools on your Mac and are not part of a standard build.

## Your own theme

A theme is the look: the font, the colours, the backdrop, the laptop or window frame, and the caption style. The built-in themes are
`paper` (soft white), `clean` (flat, one blue accent), `midnight` (deep navy), `blueprint` (white lines on blue, monospaced) and
`chalk` (chalk on a green board, handwritten).

Start your own from a built-in one:

```bash
kinhin video theme new acme --from midnight    # writes .kinhin/videos/themes/acme.yml
kinhin video theme list                        # the built-in themes and yours
```

```yaml
# .kinhin/videos/themes/acme.yml
extends: midnight            # a built-in theme, or another of yours
colors:
  accent: "#ff7a59"
  paper: "#0b1020"
font:
  family: Acme Sans          # put the font in .kinhin/videos/fonts/ and it is installed for the build
  fallback: "Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"
background:
  from: "#0b1020"
  to: "#1c2540"
```

```bash
kinhin video build launch --theme acme    # or theme: acme in the video's file
```

- **`extends`** names the theme to start from. Everything you do not write comes from it. Without `extends` the file must define
  everything: font, all seven colours, backdrop, device look and captions. Copy a built-in theme from the
  [kinhin repository](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/tree/main/video/themes) to do that.
- **Colours** are `#rrggbb`. The build checks the file and names every missing or wrong value, with the file, before anything renders.
- **The seven colours** are `ink`, `muted`, `paper`, `accent`, `card`, `track` and `line`.
- A theme file named like a built-in (`paper.yml`) replaces that theme for your videos. Names use letters, digits, `-` and `_`.
- A video's own `overrides` still apply on top of its theme.

## Scene types

Each scene has an `id`, a `type`, `props`, and its words: `narration` (sentences played in order) or `cues` (each placed `at`
seconds into the scene; a cue's `say` respells what is spoken). `minLength` sets the shortest the scene may be. The voice can
only make it longer.

| Type | Shows | Props |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | A mark that draws itself, a title, a subtitle | `title`, `subtitle`, `mark` (`ring` or `none`) |
| `statement` | One big sentence and a line under it | `text`, `sub`, `size` |
| `queue` | A queue of jobs waiting for one runner | `runner`, `count`, `caption`, `caption2` |
| `parallel` | Items each getting their own fresh card, running side by side, then vanishing | `items`, `card`, `caption`, `done` |
| `map` | Things on the left, things on the right, one hub between them | `left`, `right`, `caption`, `note` |
| `outro` | A closing line, a URL and a row of facts | `line`, `url`, `facts` |
| `stats` | Big numbers that count up (`75%`, `4`, `1.5x`, `$12` keep their prefix and suffix) | `items` (`{value, label}`), `caption` |
| `steps` | A numbered list that fills in one step at a time | `title`, `steps` |
| `code` | A code or terminal block that types itself. `$` and `>` lines are commands, `#` and `//` lines are comments | `label`, `lines`, `caption` |
| `compare` | Two cards, before and after (stacked in portrait and square frames) | `left`, `right` (each `{title, items}`), `caption` |
| `device` | A screen recording in a MacBook frame (drawn, no Apple artwork) that tilts and slides in | `clip`, `frame` (`macbook`, `window` or `none`), `speed` (a number, or [speed ramps](#speed-ramps)) |
| `terminal` | A terminal recording in a window | `clip`, `frame` (`window` or `none`) |
| `split` | Two recordings side by side (one above the other in a vertical or square frame) | `left`, `right` (each a clip with its own [camera](#camera-on-recordings), `speed` and `delay`), `ratio` |

The first ten rows are **drawn scenes**: they need no recording. `device`, `terminal` and `split` show clips from your
[adapter](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-adapters.md). An app clip defaults to the laptop frame; a browser or terminal clip defaults to a window.

A small example that mixes drawn and recorded scenes:

```yaml
scenes:
  - { id: hello, type: title, props: { title: Acme, subtitle: Ship faster }, narration: Acme helps your team ship faster. }
  - { id: steps, type: steps, props: { title: Get started, steps: [Install, Init, Build] }, narration: Three steps. }
  - { id: app,   type: device, props: { clip: app }, narration: This is the app. }
```

The `device` scene needs an adapter with a clip named `app`. Without one, the build stops and names the missing clip.

## Camera on recordings

A `device` or `terminal` scene can move a camera over its recording, spotlight part of the screen and show a cursor. The picture
inside the laptop or window moves; the frame itself holds still. Every position is a fraction of the recording, from 0 (left or
top) to 1 (right or bottom), so one script works in every format. All three props are optional and combine.

```yaml
- id: fleet
  type: device
  props:
    clip: app
    camera:                                    # zoom and pan
      - { at: 2, zoom: 1.8, to: [0.62, 0.35] }
      - { at: 6, zoom: 1 }
    focus:                                     # dim everything but a box
      - { from: 2, to: 5, box: [0.5, 0.2, 0.8, 0.5] }
    cursor:                                    # a pointer, and a ring where it clicks
      - { at: 2.2, to: [0.7, 0.3] }
      - { at: 3, to: [0.7, 0.3], click: true }
  narration: Here the fleet scales to the queue.
```

| Prop | What it does |
|---|---|
| `camera` | A list of keyframes. At `at` seconds into the scene the camera moves (`move` seconds, 0.8 by default) to `zoom` (1 to 4) centred on `to`, then holds. A keyframe without `zoom` or `to` keeps the one before it. The camera starts at zoom 1, centred. |
| `focus` | A box (or a list of them): `{from, to, box: [x0, y0, x1, y1], dim}`. Between `from` and `to` seconds everything outside the box is dimmed (`dim`, 0.55 by default, up to 0.9), fading in and out. |
| `cursor` | A list of points: `{at, to, click}`. The pointer is at `to` at `at` seconds, travelling from the point before (it sets off up to a second early). `click: true` spreads a ring from the point. Skip it if your recording already shows its own cursor. |

Anywhere a point or a box goes, you can write the name of a **target** instead, a named box of the clip that its adapter
declares (`targets` in [Recordings](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-adapters.md#recording-clips)):

```yaml
camera:  [ { at: 2, target: fleet } ]          # zoom to fit the fleet card, centred on it
focus:   { from: 2, to: 5, box: fleet }        # spotlight it
cursor:  [ { at: 2.2, to: fleet } ]            # the pointer goes to its centre
```

A keyframe's `target` sets `to` and, unless you give a `zoom`, the zoom that fits the box. When the layout of your product changes,
you fix the box once in the adapter and every video follows. `kinhin video validate` names a target that the clip does not have.

### Zoom on the clicks (autoZoom)

`autoZoom: true` (or `{zoom, lead, hold, gap, reach}`) moves the camera for you. It reads the clicks in the clip's pointer log,
`<clip>-pointer.json`, and zooms in on each burst of clicks, then zooms back out. The picture still never shows the pointer.

```yaml
- id: fleet
  type: device
  props:
    clip: app
    autoZoom: true                             # or { zoom: 1.6, lead: 0.6, hold: 1.5, gap: 3, reach: 0.35 }
  narration: Here the fleet scales to the queue.
```

| Setting | What it does (default) |
|---|---|
| `zoom` | How far the camera zooms on a burst of clicks, from 1 to 4 (1.6) |
| `lead` | Seconds before the first click that the zoom starts (0.6) |
| `hold` | Seconds after the last click that the camera stays zoomed (1.5) |
| `gap` | Clicks further apart in time than this make a new burst (3) |
| `reach` | Clicks further apart on the picture than this (a fraction, 0.35) make a new burst |

The log is written by `kinhin video record --pointer PATH` (`record-app.sh` passes it), and `make-reference.sh` carries it into
the committed reference clip. It is only where the pointer was and where it clicked, so a take with no clicks gives no zoom: click
where you want the camera to go while you record. `autoZoom` is camera work of its own, so it does not go with `camera`.

Times are seconds into the scene, after `speed` is applied. The scene's frame, captions and narration are unchanged. Recordings are
drawn at their own resolution, so a zoom of 2 or more is sharpest on a recording made at a high resolution.

## Speed ramps

A recording can play fast through the waiting and slow down for the moment that matters. `speed` is a number (any positive one), or a list of
segments. Each segment plays at its own `speed` up to `until`, a second of the recording counted from where its story starts
(the last segment has no `until` and plays to the end of the scene):

```yaml
- id: boot
  type: device
  props:
    clip: app
    speed: [ { until: 20, speed: 8 }, { until: 30, speed: 1 }, { speed: 4 } ]
    ramp: 0.4                                  # seconds to ease between speeds (default 0.4; 0 jumps)
```

Each speed in the list is from 0.1 to 30. Where the speed changes it eases over `ramp` seconds, through speeds in between, so a jump from 8x to 1x reads as the recording
slowing down. The scene lasts at least as long as its closed segments take to play (in the example, 20/8 + 10 seconds and the two
eases), however short the narration. Camera times count the scene's own seconds, after the ramps. Speed lists work in every frame.

## Split screen

A `split` scene plays two recordings at once, such as a command in a terminal and the app reacting to it. In a 16:9 frame they
sit side by side; in a vertical or square frame the first is above the second.

```yaml
- id: both
  type: split
  props:
    left:  { clip: demo }
    right: { clip: app, delay: 1.5, speed: [ { until: 3, speed: 3 }, { speed: 1 } ], camera: [ { at: 3, target: centre } ] }
    ratio: 0.5
  narration: The command on the left, and what it does on the right.
```

| Prop | What it does |
|---|---|
| `left`, `right` | Each is a clip of your adapter with the props a `device` scene takes: `camera`, `focus`, `cursor`, `speed`, `ramp`. `frame` is `window` (a title bar) or `none`; the default is `none` for a recorded app, which has its own window, and `window` for anything else. |
| `delay` | Seconds a recording waits on its first frame before it plays, to line it up with the other. |
| `ratio` | The left (or top) window's share of the room, 0.3 to 0.7. 0.5 by default. |

Each recording is its own file, so lining up cause and effect is up to you: record them together, or use `delay` and `speed` to
match them. Captions sit at the bottom, as on a terminal scene.

## Transitions

By default each scene fades out through the backdrop colour and the next fades in. A project's `transition` changes every cut;
a scene's own `transition` is how it comes in from the scene before it.

| Transition | What you see |
|---|---|
| `fade` | A dip through the backdrop colour (the default). |
| `dissolve` | A cross-dissolve. |
| `push` | The next scene pushes the last one out to the left. |
| `slide` | The next scene slides up over the last one. |
| `wipe` | A hard-edged wipe from the right. |
| `circle` | The next scene opens from the middle in a circle. |

```yaml
transition: dissolve          # every cut, unless a scene says otherwise
scenes:
  - { id: intro, type: title, props: { title: Acme }, narration: Meet Acme. }
  - { id: app, type: device, transition: push, props: { clip: app }, narration: This is the app. }
```

A transition lasts half a second (less between very short scenes) and is centred on the cut, so no scene moves on the clock and
the narration stays in step. The first scene has nothing to come in from.

## Captions

A video writes two caption outputs. The **caption file** (`out/<name>/<name>.srt`, every cue) is written on every build for a
player. **Burned-in** captions are drawn on the picture. Turn them on or off, and choose their style, in the file:

```json
"captions": { "burn": true, "scenes": "clips", "style": "box", "position": "auto", "size": 1.1, "color": "#ffffff" }
```

| Setting | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `burn` | `true`, `false`, or the formats to burn them in, such as `["9:16", "1:1"]` (clean in the others) | `true` (an adapter can set `false` or a list) |
| `scenes` | `"clips"` (scenes with no text of their own), `"all"`, or a list of scene ids | `"clips"` |
| `style` | `outline` (text with an outline), `box` (a semi-transparent box), `shadow` (a soft drop shadow), `bold` (larger, bold, outlined), `minimal` (small, plain), `karaoke` (bold and outlined, each word lights up as it is spoken) | `outline` (`box` if the theme asks for one) |
| `position` | `auto` (clear of the laptop or window), `bottom`, `top`, `middle` | `auto` |
| `size` | A multiplier, up to 3 | `1` |
| `color`, `outlineColor`, `boxColor`, `font` | `#rrggbb` (`#rrggbbaa` for opacity); a font name | from the theme |
| `highlightColor` | `karaoke` only: the colour of the words already spoken (the rest are `color`, dimmed) | `color` |
| `sidecar` | `true` or `false` | `true` |

```bash
kinhin video build launch --captions off                 # a clean picture; the .srt is still written
kinhin video build launch --captions all                 # burn them into every scene
kinhin video build launch --caption-style box            # outline, box, shadow, bold, minimal or karaoke
```

`karaoke` times each word from its length within the narrated sentence, since the voice reports a sentence at a time, so the light
follows the speech closely but not to the syllable. It suits short sentences and vertical formats best. The caption file is the
same as for every other style.

Later settings win: the theme, then the adapter's `captions` block, then the video's, then the command line. The
[gallery](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-gallery.md#captions) shows every style.

## Music

Nothing plays unless an adapter or the video selects a track. The quickest way to add one is to search for it:

```bash
kinhin video music search "calm piano"          # CC0 and public-domain tracks; the rows are numbered
kinhin video music preview 3                    # listen to row 3 (macOS)
kinhin video music add 3 --video launch         # download it and set music: in .kinhin/videos/launch.yml
kinhin video music list                         # what each video uses, and which saved tracks are unused
```

- **Where results come from.** [Openverse](https://openverse.org), an index of openly licensed audio (mostly Freesound, also
  Wikimedia Commons), plus the tracks built into the video image. No account is needed. Anonymous use allows about 200 searches
  a day.
- **Licences.** Results are CC0 or public domain by default: no credit needed. `--license cc-by` also shows CC BY tracks, which
  need credit. Tracks with a non-commercial, no-derivatives or share-alike condition are never offered.
- **More searches.** Register a free application with Openverse and set `KINHIN_OPENVERSE_CLIENT_ID` and
  `KINHIN_OPENVERSE_CLIENT_SECRET` in your environment for a higher allowance. They are read from the environment only and
  never written to a file.
- **Short loops.** Many results are short loops, which work because the video loops music. Some are sound effects.
  `--min-seconds` (default 20) and `--max-seconds` narrow the results.
- **What `add` does.** It saves the audio to `.kinhin/videos/music/<name>.mp3`, writes `<name>.json` beside it (title, creator,
  source page, licence, SHA-256), and sets `music:` in the video's YAML, leaving the rest of the file and its comments alone.
  With one video in the folder it is chosen for you; with several, name it with `--video`. `--volume` sets the level
  (default 0.35), and `--no-config` only downloads and prints the block. A JSON config is not rewritten: the block is printed
  for you to paste.
- **Credit.** For a CC BY track, `add` writes the credit into `credit:`, and the build saves it to `out/<name>/music-credit.txt`.
  Put it in your video description.
- **Your responsibility.** Licences are as each source declares them. Check the track's page (`preview` prints it) before you
  publish, and keep the `.json` record with the audio.

### The setting

```yaml
music:
  track: .kinhin/videos/music/calm-piano.mp3   # a file in your repository, a catalog name, or an https URL (with sha256)
  volume: 0.35         # before ducking under the voice
  duck: true           # lower it while the narrator speaks
  fadeIn: 2
  fadeOut: 3
  start: 0             # seconds into the track
  loop: true
  credit: "..."        # written to out/<name>/music-credit.txt
```

`track` is one of three things:

- a **file** in your repository (mp3, m4a, wav, flac or ogg);
- a **catalog name** (`first-light-particles` ships in the image, CC0, so a build needs no network);
- an **https URL** with `sha256`. The download is refused if it does not match.

`music: path/to/track.mp3` is short for `{track: ...}`, and `music: false` turns off a track an adapter selects. Later settings
win: adapter, then video, then the command line or environment (`--music <track|file|URL|off>`, `VIDEO_MUSIC`,
`VIDEO_MUSIC_SHA256`, `VIDEO_MUSIC_VOLUME`, `NO_MUSIC=1`).

A track you supply is your responsibility to have the right to use.

## Build flags

```bash
kinhin video build launch                                   # your .kinhin/videos/launch.yml
kinhin video build launch --fast                            # a preview: quicker encode, no WebM
kinhin video build launch --quality high --fps 60            # slower, larger encode at 60 fps
kinhin video build launch --theme midnight --format 9:16    # another look or frame, without editing the file
kinhin video build launch --runtime docker                  # pick the runtime
```

The render cache is `.kinhin/videos/.cache`. A scene is re-rendered only when something that shapes it changed: its type and
props, its length, the theme, the format, or the scene sources. A second build after editing one line re-renders one scene.
Delete the cache to render everything again. How a build works step by step is in
[making a video](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/making-a-video.md#how-the-build-works).

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-adapters.md

# Recordings of your product

A **device**, **terminal** or **split** scene shows recordings of your product. You do not need recording tools to use a clip you
already have. This page covers the adapter folder that holds the recordings, the claims check that keeps the video honest,
and the optional web recorder.

[← Back to Add videos to your project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md) · [Config reference](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md) · [Troubleshooting](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-troubleshooting.md)

**On this page:** [The adapter folder](#the-adapter-folder) · [Recording clips](#recording-clips) · [Settings an adapter can carry](#settings-an-adapter-can-carry) ·
[Keep it honest](#keep-it-honest) · [Record a web product](#record-a-web-product)

## The adapter folder

An adapter is a folder, `.kinhin/videos/adapters/<name>/`, with an `adapter.yml` that names the clips and a `reference/`
folder that holds them. A video uses it with `adapter: <name>`.

```
.kinhin/videos/adapters/acme/
├── adapter.yml          which clips there are, and settings for every video that uses the adapter
├── claims.json          optional: what your videos must not say (see Keep it honest)
└── reference/
    ├── app.mp4          a screen recording of your app
    └── demo.mp4         a terminal session
```

```yaml
# .kinhin/videos/adapters/acme/adapter.yml
name: acme
description: Acme's own recordings.
captions: { burn: ["9:16", "1:1"] }   # optional (kinhin's own adapter sets burn: false and never burns captions): settings for every video that uses this adapter
clips:
  app:  { kind: app }           # a screen recording of the product      -> reference/app.mp4
  demo: { kind: terminal }      # a terminal session                     -> reference/demo.mp4
  site: { kind: browser }       # a web page being used                  -> reference/site.mp4
```

A video then uses the clips by name:

```yaml
# .kinhin/videos/tour.yml
name: Acme tour
adapter: acme
scenes:
  - { id: app, type: device,   props: { clip: app },  narration: This is the app. }
  - { id: cli, type: terminal, props: { clip: demo }, narration: And this is the command line. }
```

A scene that names a clip the adapter does not declare stops the build and names the scene and the clip.

## Recording clips

Record each clip with anything you like, and save it as `reference/<clip>.mp4`:

- **App:** `kinhin video record <app>` on a Mac (one window, pointer left out; needs Screen Recording permission for your terminal once), or QuickTime. Add `--pointer <clip>-pointer.json` to keep where the pointer was and where it clicked, which a video's [autoZoom](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md#zoom-on-the-clicks-autozoom) follows. Copy that `<clip>-pointer.json` into `reference/` beside the clip, since autoZoom reads it from there.
- **Terminal:** [VHS](https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs), or any terminal recorder that writes an MP4.
- **Website or browser:** any browser recorder. See [Record a web product](#record-a-web-product) for a scripted option.

H.264 is fine. A few hundred KB to a few MB each is small enough to commit.

- **Where the story starts.** An app clip may have a `<clip>.json` beside it, `{"demoStartsAt": 4.5}`. That is the second into
  the recording where the interesting part begins, so the scene skips what comes before.
- **Named regions (targets).** A clip in `adapter.yml` may name boxes of its picture, as `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` from 0 to 1 across the
  recording: `app: { kind: app, targets: { fleet: [0.17, 0.69, 0.83, 0.94] } }`. A video's [camera, focus and cursor](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md#camera-on-recordings)
  can then say `target: fleet` instead of coordinates, so a redesigned screen is fixed once, here.
- **Terminal variants.** A terminal clip may come in four looks, chosen by the theme's `terminal` mode (`light` or `dark`) and
  the format: `demo.mp4`, `demo-dark.mp4`, `demo-portrait.mp4` and `demo-dark-portrait.mp4`. A missing variant falls back to the
  plain one.

## Settings an adapter can carry

`captions` and `music` in `adapter.yml` apply to every video that uses the adapter (the same blocks as a video's, see
[Captions](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md#captions) and [Music](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md#music)). A video's own settings win.

An adapter can also select a music track for all its videos, and can choose the formats that get burned-in captions. A video can bring them back
with its own `captions` block or `--captions on`.

## Keep it honest

A video is a claim. Say only what your product does today. The build checks the narration, the timed cues and every string in a
scene's props against an adapter's `claims.json` **before anything renders**:

```json
{
  "planned": ["Windows", "Azure Pipelines"],
  "plannedMarkers": ["planned", "roadmap", "coming soon"],
  "forbidden": ["fastest", "enterprise-grade", "revolutionary"]
}
```

- **`planned`** lists names on your roadmap that you have not shipped. A sentence may mention one only if it also says it is
  planned (one of the `plannedMarkers`). "Windows support is planned." passes; "Runs on Windows." fails.
- **`forbidden`** lists words you never want said or shown, such as superlatives you cannot back up.
- A video can add its own rules with a `claims:` block of the same shape.
- A failure names the scene and the text, and stops the build before the voice-over starts.

Put numbers on screen only when you can point at where they come from, and say when they come from one machine.

## Record a web product

This recorder runs from a checkout of the [kinhin repository](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin), because it needs host
tools. It is optional: any recording of a web page works. Copy the finished clip into your adapter's `reference/` folder.

```bash
video/scripts/record-web.sh --scenario adapters/kinhin/scenarios/site.json --runner local \
  --serve "npm --prefix website run preview -- --port 4173"
```

`--runner docker` or `--runner apple` runs the same thing in the official Playwright image (Docker, or Apple's `container run`),
so the recording never depends on the host's browser or fonts. The product must be reachable from inside that container: `--serve`
starts it there, or use a public URL. `localhost` on the host is not `localhost` in the container. Set `PACE=0.5` to play a
scenario twice as fast, and `BASE_URL` to point it elsewhere.

A scenario is JSON. Copy `video/adapters/kinhin/scenarios/site.json` to start:

```json
{ "baseUrl": "http://localhost:4173", "viewport": { "width": 1920, "height": 1080 }, "colorScheme": "light",
  "steps": [
    { "do": "goto", "url": "/" },
    { "do": "scroll", "y": 700, "ms": 2200 },
    { "do": "click", "text": "Get started" },
    { "do": "type", "selector": "input[name=q]", "text": "hello", "delayMs": 80 }
  ] }
```

Steps: `goto` (relative to `baseUrl`), `wait` (`ms`), `move`, `hover`, `click`, `type`, `press` (`key`) and `scroll` (`y` pixels,
or `selector`; `ms` is the duration, eased). Target an element with `selector` (CSS or Playwright selectors) or `text`. The page
shows a visible cursor, because Playwright's recording does not draw one. A failing step stops the run with its number and
writes no file.

Other recorders (`record-clip.mjs`, `record-terminal.sh`, `make-reference.sh`) and an `adapters/template/` that records synthetic
clips are in the kinhin repository's `video/` folder, for scripted and repeatable recordings. Their manifest keys are described in
`video/scripts/adapter.mjs`.

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting videos

The messages a video build is most likely to print, and what to do. Find the text your build printed in the left column.

[← Back to Add videos to your project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md) · [Config reference](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md) · [Recordings](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-adapters.md)

The build prints the pipeline's own output as it runs. Read the whole log, not only the last line: the line above the failure
usually says why. `kinhin doctor` checks your container runtimes.

| You see | What to do |
|---|---|
| `videos build in a container, and neither Apple's container nor Docker is running` | Start one: `container system start` (install with `brew install container`), or open Docker Desktop. `--runtime container` or `--runtime docker` forces one and says why it is not usable. |
| `kinhin video validate` lists problems and exits 3 | Each line names the scene or setting and what is wrong. Nothing was rendered, so fix the file and run `kinhin video validate` again. |
| `this video image predates 'kinhin video validate'` | The image for your kinhin version is older than the check. Update kinhin, or pass `--image` with a newer image. |
| `no .kinhin/videos/ in <path>` or `no video "x"` | You are in the wrong directory, or the file is missing. `kinhin video list` shows what is found. `kinhin video init x` creates it. `--dir PATH` points at another repository. |
| `could not get the video image ghcr.io/...` | Check the network. The image for your kinhin version must be published: a development build of kinhin has no published image, so pass `--image` or set `KINHIN_VIDEO_IMAGE`. If the package is private, sign in with `docker login ghcr.io`. |
| The build stops with a message from the pipeline | The log above the final line says why: a scene with no `id`, an unknown theme (the message lists the ones that exist), a clip that is not in the adapter, or a claim that `claims.json` forbids. Fix the config and run the build again. Scenes you did not change come from the render cache, so the rerun is fast. |
| `no space left` or `read-only file system` | The image is about 1 GB and a build needs a few GB free. Free disk space. Apple's `container` keeps its images and builder cache under your home folder; `docker system prune` frees Docker's. |
| `scene "x": no clip "app" in the acme adapter` | The adapter does not declare that clip, or its file is missing. Add the clip to `.kinhin/videos/adapters/<name>/adapter.yml` and put the recording at `reference/<clip>.mp4` (a terminal clip may also have `-dark`, `-portrait` and `-dark-portrait` variants). See [Recordings](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-adapters.md#the-adapter-folder). |
| `theme "x": ... is missing` or `... must be a colour` | A theme file in `.kinhin/videos/themes/` is incomplete. Add `extends: midnight` (or another theme) and write only what you change. Colours are `#rrggbb`. The message names every problem at once. See [Your own theme](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md#your-own-theme). |
| `"Windows" is planned, not shipped` (a claims failure) | A scene mentions something your `claims.json` lists as planned without saying so, or it uses a forbidden word. Reword the line, or say that it is planned. See [Keep it honest](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-adapters.md#keep-it-honest). |
| A music file or font is not found | Paths are relative to your repository, and the repository is mounted read-only in the container. Check that the file is committed and inside the repository, and that its extension is mp3, m4a, wav, flac or ogg. Fonts go in `.kinhin/videos/fonts/`. |
| `music search` says the library is rate limiting | Anonymous use allows about 20 searches a minute and 200 a day. Wait, or set `KINHIN_OPENVERSE_CLIENT_ID` and `KINHIN_OPENVERSE_CLIENT_SECRET` from a free Openverse application. Tracks built into the image still show up offline. |
| `add` refuses a track: `is licensed ..., which kinhin does not put in a video` | Only CC0 and public-domain tracks are accepted, and CC BY with `--license cc-by`. Non-commercial, no-derivatives and share-alike tracks are never added. Pick another result. |
| `add` says `which video?` or `there is no video` | Name the video with `--video <name>` when the folder has several, or run `kinhin video init` first. `--no-config` only downloads the track. |
| `did not download the track` | The file is over 50 MB, is not mp3, m4a, wav, flac or ogg, is not served over https, or its source link is gone. Try another result. `preview` shows the source page. |
| `--on-fleet`: `kinhin-video.yml is not on <branch>` | Run `kinhin video init --workflow`, commit and push the file, then try again. `--on-fleet` also needs `gh` signed in (`gh auth login`) and a runner with Docker that matches `--runs-on`. |

| A rebuild shows an old picture or voice | Framed recordings, drawn scenes and the voice of each sentence are reused while nothing that shapes them has changed. If one is stale, delete `.kinhin/videos/.cache/` (or just its `frames/`, `scenes/` or `voice-cache/` folder) and build again. With `video/scripts/build.sh`, `RENDER_FORCE=1` (pictures) and `VOICE_FORCE=1` (voice) do the same for one build. |
| `no scene "x" in this video (its scenes: ...)` | `--scene` takes scene ids from the video's file, comma-separated. The message lists them. |

Builds feel slow? Every build prints how long each step took. Try `--scene` and `--watch` while iterating (see [Faster rebuilds](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md#faster-rebuilds)). `kinhin bench video` times the image pull, a clean build and a cached rebuild on this Mac; see [Benchmarks](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/benchmarks.md).

Still stuck? Open an issue with the full build log, with any token or key removed.

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-gallery.md

# Video gallery

Every video below is built from a JSON file in `video/script/` with one command, in a container, from committed sources. Each picture is a
frame from each scene of the real build. To make one of your own, copy a file into your repository's `.kinhin/videos/` and run
`kinhin video build <name>` (see [Add videos to your project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md)). `video/scripts/gallery.mjs` rebuilds all of this
page and writes a page where you can play the videos.

[← Back to README](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/index.md) · [Add videos to your project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md) · [Marketing video in CI](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/ci-video.md)

## Captions

The same scene with captions off and in each style. Burned-in captions are a project setting (`captions` in the JSON) or a flag
(`--captions off`, `--caption-style box`); the caption file is written either way. See
[Captions](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md#captions).

### Captions off

No burned-in captions; the .srt is still written.

![Captions off: a frame from each scene](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RabinApps/kinhin/v0.0.1-beta-4/docs/assets/video-gallery/captions-off.jpg)

16:9 · clean theme · 33 s · 5 scenes (title, device, terminal, outro)

```bash

```

### Captions: outline

Text with a contrasting outline (the default).

![Captions: outline: a frame from each scene](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RabinApps/kinhin/v0.0.1-beta-4/docs/assets/video-gallery/captions-outline.jpg)


# Marketing video in CI (opt-in)

The video suite ([Add videos to your project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md)) can build a launch video, social cuts and a preview of video
changes in GitHub Actions, from committed sources, with no secrets. It is **off by default**: a repository that does not
opt in gets no jobs, no cost and no new permissions.

[← Back to README](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/index.md) · [Add videos to your project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md) · [The plan behind it](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/v0.0.1-beta-4/docs/plans/marketing-suite-in-ci.md)

## Switch it on

Three switches, all off until you flip them:

1. **Repository variable.** Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables → `VIDEO_CI` = `true`. Without it every
   job in the Video workflow is skipped. This is the kill switch: set it back to `false` to stop everything.
2. **`video/ci.json`.** Set `"enabled": true`, then turn on the triggers you want (`triggers.release`,
   `triggers.pullRequest`, `triggers.schedule`). A manual run does not need `enabled`.
3. **The `marketing` environment** (Settings → Environments). Add required reviewers. Publishing (attaching to a release,
   opening a site pull request) waits for approval there, and only runs when `publish.release` or `publish.site` is `true`.

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "triggers": { "release": true, "pullRequest": false, "schedule": false },
  "projects": [
    { "project": "launch", "looks": [{}, { "theme": "midnight", "format": "9:16" }, { "format": "4:5" }] }
  ],
  "publish": { "release": true, "site": false },
  "budgets": { "mp4MB": 10, "seconds": 90, "buildMinutes": 20 }
}
```

## What runs, and when

| Trigger | When | Builds | Publishes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Manual** (Actions → Video → Run workflow) | You pick project, theme, format, adapter | Exactly that, one look | Nothing: download the artifact |
| **Release** (`triggers.release`) | After the Release workflow succeeds for a tag | Every look in `projects` (the launch video, a vertical cut, a 4:5 cut) | The release (`publish.release`) and a site pull request (`publish.site`), each behind the `marketing` environment |
| **Pull request** (`triggers.pullRequest`) | A same-repository PR with the `video-preview` label, or one that changes a `previewPaths` file | The `preview` set, fast (a quicker encode) | Nothing: artifact and a job summary |
| **Schedule** (`triggers.schedule`) | The first of each month | Every look in `projects` | Nothing |

Pull requests from forks never build. Nothing here needs a secret: the build uses the workflow's read-only token, and only
the two publish jobs get `contents: write` (and `pull-requests: write` for the site pull request).

## The jobs

```
plan ──► claims ──► build (one job per look) ──► publish-release / publish-site (reviewed)
```

- **plan** decides whether to build and what, in seconds.
- **claims** is the honesty gate: it fails when a video says something the product does not support (for kinhin, any of the
  planned platforms such as Buildkite or Windows without saying they are planned, and tone words like "fastest"). The rules
  live in the adapter (`video/adapters/<name>/claims.json`) and the project file.
- **build** runs `video/scripts/build.sh --container --runtime docker` on a hosted Linux runner (the same command you run
  locally), then **verifies** the result and writes a summary table. A release build pulls the image published for that release
  (`ghcr.io/rabinapps/kinhin-video:<version>`, made by `video-image.yml`) instead of building it once per look; a pull request,
  a manual run, or a release whose image is not published yet builds it from the checked-out sources.
- **verify** is the same checker the end-to-end tests use (`video/scripts/verify.mjs`): the frame size, the length against the
  timeline, an audio track near -16 LUFS, no black frames, one caption per cue, a poster and a hero GIF that are not blank, and
  the size and length budgets. A video that fails is not published.

A failed video job never blocks a release, a docs deploy or a pull request: nothing depends on it.

## Store screenshots in the mobile cut

`examples/mobile-30s` is a launch cut that shows store screenshots. Its look sets `"screens": true` in `video/ci.json`, so
the plan adds one job before the build:

- **`mobile-capture`** runs on the macOS pool (`kinhin-xcode`), because the iOS simulator needs macOS. It generates the iOS
  example, runs `bundle exec fastlane screenshots` for `en-US` and `fr-FR`, and uploads the PNGs as the `mobile-screens`
  artifact. Only looks that set `screens` run it; other builds are unchanged.
- **`build`** (Linux, in the container) downloads `mobile-screens` into `video/screens/mobile/` for that look only, then
  renders. The cut's `device` scenes point at those files with `props.screens` (see [making a video](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/making-a-video.md#screenshots-as-a-scene)).

There is one capture job per platform a look needs (`ios` and `android`), and each look picks its platform in `video/ci.json`.
The Android capture boots the pool's emulator (`KINHIN_AVD`, default `Pixel_9`) and needs its system image on the runner; the
iOS capture is verified locally, the Android one is not yet verified on the pool.

## Your own product's videos on your fleet

`kinhin video build <name> --on-fleet` runs a video of *your* repository on a runner kinhin serves, with no `video/` folder:
`kinhin video init --workflow` writes `.github/workflows/kinhin-video.yml` (pinned actions, read-only token, no secrets), and
`--on-fleet` dispatches it with `gh`, follows the run and downloads the result. See
[Building on your fleet](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md#building-on-a-runner-or-in-ci). The opt-in `video.yml` described on this page is a
different thing: it builds *kinhin's* own videos from this repository.

## Try it without GitHub

The decisions are a script you can run here:

```bash
cd video
node scripts/video-ci.mjs validate                        # is ci.json valid?
node scripts/video-claims-lint.mjs --all                  # does every video say only true things?
VIDEO_CI=true GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=workflow_dispatch INPUT_PROJECT=launch \
  node scripts/video-ci.mjs plan                          # what would a manual run build?
scripts/build.sh --container --project examples/hello     # the build itself
node scripts/video-ci.mjs verify out                      # the checks, on a finished build
```

`scripts/video-check.sh` runs the first two plus the unit tests, and `scripts/check.sh` and the CI docs job run it on every
change. See [the tests](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/making-a-video.md#tests) (kinhin's own guide).

## Use it for another product

Do not copy `video.yml`: it builds *kinhin's own* videos from this repository. For your product, keep your videos in `.kinhin/videos/`
and build them with `kinhin video build` on your Mac, or on your fleet with `kinhin video init --workflow` and `--on-fleet` (see
[Add videos to your project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md#building-on-a-runner-or-in-ci)). That generated workflow is manual (`workflow_dispatch`)
and pulls the published video image, so you need no `video/` folder; to build on every release, add a `release:` trigger to it yourself.

## When something fails

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| The workflow shows every job skipped | `VIDEO_CI` is not `true`, or `ci.json` has `"enabled": false`, or the trigger's switch is off. The plan job's log says which. |
| `claims` fails | A scene mentions something the adapter's `claims.json` lists as planned, or a tone word. The message names the scene and the text. |
| `build` fails in `verify` | The log lists each failed check (size, length, loudness, black frames, captions). Budgets are in `ci.json`. |
| A pull request got no preview | It is from a fork, or has neither the `video-preview` label nor a changed `previewPaths` file. |
| `publish-*` waits | It is waiting for approval in the `marketing` environment. |

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

Start with `kinhin heal`: the [healing agent](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/healing.md) fixes many of the problems below on its own, lists the
fixes waiting for your approval, and says what only you can do.

- **`kinhin doctor` shows "tart: NOT FOUND"** — run `kinhin setup repair tart` (or use the setup
  window's fix button), then re-run `kinhin doctor`.
- **"tart: INSTALLED BUT KILLED ON LAUNCH ✗"** — the OpenAI-tap bottle is un-notarized;
  Gatekeeper kills it before it runs. `kinhin doctor` and the setup app print/offer the exact
  rollback commands; the manual equivalents are in [Installing Tart](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md#installing-tart).
- **Jobs queue but no VMs start** — check that the job's `runs-on:` contains _every_ label in
  your config; the scaler only counts jobs it could actually run.
- **Scale set: `runner group 'default' was not found; create it in GitHub before attaching`** —
  with `scale_set:` on a GitHub account, kinhin looks the runner group up by an exact,
  case-sensitive name, and its default (`default`) is not GitHub's built-in group name
  (`Default`), so no scale set is ever created and the listener retries forever. Set
  `runner_group: "Default"` under `scale_set:` in `config.yaml`, spelled exactly as GitHub
  spells it, then restart the app — account-level config is not live-reloaded. Walkthrough:
  [Troubleshooting scale sets](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges/github.md#troubleshooting-scale-sets).
- **VM boots but the runner never registers** — the base image may predate the injected agent.
  Re-run `kinhin image prepare`. Full logs: `kinhin logs -n 200` or
  `~/Library/Application Support/Kinhin/logs/kinhin.log`.
- **`lifecycle failed: runner registration failed … ssh: connect to host <ip> port 22: Operation timed out`** —
  the fresh VM booted and got an IP, but its SSH server did not answer within the bring-up window
  (at least `vm_boot_timeout`, default 300s). Common causes: the **first boot of a freshly prepared
  image** (macOS first-boot work can delay sshd for minutes — big images like full Xcode are the
  usual offenders), the host being busy with a bake or other jobs, or a softnet hiccup. kinhin
  retries the TCP/SSH probes for the whole window, then deletes the VM and scales a fresh one — the
  job normally lands on the replacement, so an isolated occurrence is harmless. If it repeats:
  raise `vm_boot_timeout` (e.g. `600`) for slow images, keep the host quiet during boot storms,
  and re-prepare the image if the guest agent is flaky on every boot.
- **Every cold start takes about 15 seconds longer than the VM needs, with the log line `port 22 probe saw nothing …; trying ssh anyway`** —
  kinhin watches a new VM's port 22 with a TCP probe before it runs ssh. On macOS, **Local Network privacy**
  can block that probe (system log: `unsatisfied (Local network prohibited)`; check with
  `log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "Local network prohibited"'`) while `/usr/bin/ssh` still
  reaches the guest, so the probe never succeeds. kinhin gives the probe 15 seconds, then tries ssh
  regardless; registration still works, you only lose the grace period. Older releases waited the whole
  `vm_boot_timeout` (about five minutes) before the first ssh. The 15-second fallback is the fix that
  matters. Release builds of the app also declare `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`, which may let macOS ask
  for Local Network access for the app process; this is unverified, and a daemon started from the CLI or a
  LaunchAgent has no app bundle for macOS to ask about. If **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local
  Network** lists kinhin, make sure it is on. Do not edit the privacy database or turn off the firewall to work
  around it.
- **Tart: `Error Domain=VZErrorDomain Code=-9 "The virtual machine encountered a security error."`** (with
  `Failed to create new HostKey`; `tart ip` then says `no IP address found, is your VM running?`) — the
  macOS login keychain's password often differs from your account password. Check it with
  `security unlock-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db`: if that says _The user name or passphrase
  you entered is not correct._, reset the keychain. In a reported case, over Screen Sharing, **Keychain
  Access → Settings → Reset My Default Keychain** fixed it. This deletes the passwords saved in the login
  keychain, so re-enter the ones you need, then confirm the kinhin token with `kinhin doctor --check-tokens`.
  Do not delete the keychain instead; that removes the same passwords without fixing the mismatch. Full
  steps: [Tart FAQ, Keychain password mismatch](https://tart.run/faq/#keychain-password-mismatch). Other
  errors such as `SecKeyCreateRandomKey_ios failed` can share this cause. Steps that did not help in the
  reported cases: reinstalling Tart, rebooting, stopping Multipass, updating the Command Line Tools.
- **`image prepare` fails while provisioning the new VM with `No route to host`, `Operation timed out` or `Host is down`** (the log line is `agent provision/update failed … could not reach the guest VM`) —
  the baked VM booted and got an IP, but the host can't open a connection to it. The usual cause is
  **OrbStack or Docker Desktop running on the same host**: their VPN/interop networking can re-route the
  virtual network interface tart uses between host and guest, so the host's `ssh` to the VM never lands.
  Quit OrbStack/Docker for the length of the bake (they can be restarted afterwards) and re-run
  `kinhin image prepare`; kinhin appends this hint to the failure message automatically. If it still fails
  with no such app running, re-run with `--verbose` and check the host's routing table
  (`netstat -rn | grep bridge`): a VPN client or firewall rewriting the VM network's interface is the
  next suspect.
- **Token rejected** — re-run `kinhin auth set`; the PAT needs `repo` scope and access to the
  repo.
- **First launch blocked** — only applies to old releases or locally built copies (official
  releases are signed and notarized). Right-click → Open, or `xattr -cr /Applications/kinhin.app`.

## Building kinhin and CI failures (for contributors)

CI builds on the `kinhin-xcode` runner with Xcode 26.5 (Swift 6.3.x). A newer Xcode on your Mac can accept code that
CI's compiler rejects or crashes on, so a green local build is not proof. Run the CI jobs on your branch and read the
log from the terminal:

```bash
gh workflow run ci.yml --ref my-branch                       # test, tsan and docs on your branch
gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch my-branch --limit 3   # find the run
gh run view <run id> --json jobs --jq '.jobs[] | "\(.name) \(.conclusion) \(.databaseId)"'
gh api repos/RabinApps/kinhin/actions/jobs/<job id>/logs --allow-escape-sequences | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' > job.log
```

- **`error: passing closure as a 'sending' parameter risks causing data races` with the note `closure captures reference to
  mutable let 'x'`** (`SendingClosureRisksDataRace`) — a local `let x = Mutex(...)` is captured by a `Task` or `addTask`
  closure that the enclosing task also uses. Swift 6.3 rejects a noncopyable `Mutex` there; newer compilers accept it.
  Use `Locked(...)` (`Sources/KinhinKit/Core/Locked.swift`) instead: same `withLock`, but a `Sendable` class. After a
  crash or an error the compiler only reports the files it reached, so convert every local `Mutex` in the file (and
  its siblings), not only the line it names.
- **`compile command failed due to signal 6`, `SmallVector unable to grow`, and `While emitting IR SIL function
  "@$s…_TR"`** — the compiler crashed building a reabstraction thunk. The one we hit came from handing a main-actor
  method to an API as a function value (`Binding(get: …, set: select)`). Pass a closure instead (`set: { select($0) }`).
  `swift demangle '<the symbol>'` names the types in the thunk, which points at the code to look for. Bisect on CI with a
  throwaway `ci-bisect/*` branch whose workflow builds one product, since the failing compiler is not on your Mac.
- **Localization tests fail only on CI** (`the compiled String Catalog is missing from …kinhin_kinhin-app.bundle`, or text
  like `1 instances` where `1 instance` is expected) — Swift 6.3's default (native) build system copies
  `Localizable.xcstrings` without compiling it, so no plural forms exist. Build and test with `--build-system swiftbuild`
  (Swift 6.4 already defaults to it). Every kinhin script and workflow passes it; add it when you run `swift test` by hand
  with a 6.3 toolchain. A release packaged without it would ship an uncompiled catalog.
- **A test passes alone and locally but fails in `swift test --parallel` on CI**, for example because it finds files another
  test left behind — parallel runs use several processes that share the machine's temp directory. Give each test its own
  directory and never assert on, or clean, the shared temp directory. `UpdateChecker(downloadRoot:)` and the update tests
  show the pattern.
- **`docs` job: `Video suite … Cannot find package 'yaml'`** — that job runs the video unit tests with Node only. The video
  scripts load `yaml` lazily (only when a YAML config is read) and `scripts/video-check.sh` runs a one-time
  `npm ci --omit=dev` when `node_modules` is missing. Do not add top-level imports of packages to scripts that the CI planner or
  the claims check import.
- **Orphaned `kinhin daemon` processes after the e2e suite** — each belongs to a `/tmp/ke2e-*` sandbox that is gone. A
  sandbox now stops its daemons when it is disposed, and `scripts/e2e-sweep.sh --force` clears the rest. Check
  `ps eww -p <pid> | tr ' ' '\n' | grep KINHIN_SUPPORT_DIR` shows a `/tmp/ke2e-…` directory before you kill one by hand.
- **Reproducing CI's compiler locally** — the swift.org 6.3.2 toolchain can be unpacked without installing it
  (`pkgutil --expand-full`), but it needs an SDK from the same generation: this Mac's macOS 27 SDK needs Swift 6.4, so the
  build fails with `unknown argument: '-target-arch-variant'`. Without Xcode 26.5's SDK, use CI as the oracle.

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/beta-roadmap.md

# Beta roadmap to v0.1.0

What is supported today, and the milestones between the current beta and the **v0.1.0** release.

[← Back to README](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/index.md) · [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md#what-has-been-tested)

kinhin is in beta (`v0.0.1-beta-4`).

The beta supports **GitHub, Gitea, Forgejo and GitLab CE**; Buildkite, Azure Pipelines and Bitbucket Pipelines follow in
later betas (planned for beta 5). Milestones are ordered by what has to be true, not by date.

## Where we are

| Area | State |
| ---- | ----- |
| GitHub Actions | Supported; live-tested on Tart macOS VMs and apple/container |
| Gitea, Forgejo, GitLab CE | Supported; live-tested on every runtime by the [end-to-end suite](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/e2e-testing.md) |
| Runtimes: Tart macOS and Linux VMs, apple/container, Docker, host mode | Live-tested |
| Buildkite, Azure Pipelines, Bitbucket Pipelines | Planned (implemented and unit-tested, not supported yet) |
| ThreadSanitizer | Clean (`scripts/tsan.sh`) |
| Long-running soak test | Not done |
| In-app updater | Ships in beta-3; not yet exercised by a published release updating itself (needs the next release) |
| Telemetry | Opt-in OpenTelemetry (off by default; exports only to a server you configure). See [Telemetry](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/telemetry.md) |

## Milestones

### beta-1: first public beta

- GitHub, Gitea, Forgejo and GitLab CE supported. Gitea, Forgejo and GitLab CE live-tested on every runtime; GitHub on
  Tart macOS VMs and apple/container.
- Menu bar app, CLI and LaunchAgent daemon released, signed and notarized.
- Docs, forge reference and the forge-report issue template published.

### beta-2: hardening the supported forges

- Fixes from beta testers' real projects.
- The GitHub lane of the end-to-end suite running against a throwaway repository.
- The e2e suite running nightly on a dedicated Mac.
- Exercise the in-app updater against a published release.

**Exit:** no open bugs that lose a job or leak a runner on a supported forge.

### beta-3: updater, restart safety and localization

- The in-app updater installs updates itself (Sparkle, EdDSA-signed feed).
- A restart no longer registers a VM again while its runner is still on the forge.
- Ollama as a healing advisor, camera and karaoke captions for videos, and the app in seven more languages.
- Azure Pipelines labeled experimental.

### beta-4: telemetry, macOS 27 images and reliability (current)

- Opt-in OpenTelemetry: metrics, traces and logs over OTLP, a Prometheus endpoint, `kinhin telemetry status` and a menu bar card.
- The macOS 27 Golden Gate base images and digest-pinned base images.
- Install and reliability fixes: the daemon's LaunchAgent path, `vm.cpu` and `vm.memory_gb` on Tart, warm-pool counting, and
  every running job shown on multi-runner VMs.
- Linux runners (Apple container and Docker) no longer carry the `macos` label.

The Buildkite, Azure Pipelines and Bitbucket Pipelines work promised for this beta did not make it and moves to beta 5.

### beta-5: more forges

- Buildkite, Azure Pipelines and Bitbucket Pipelines run against real accounts in the end-to-end suite, and become
  supported one by one as they pass.
- Multi-account and mixed-forge fleets on one shared pool.
- Register the dedicated `kinhin-e2e` Mac, run the GitHub lane, and turn on the nightly end-to-end run.

**Exit:** every forge the docs call supported is live-tested; the rest are clearly labeled planned.

### rc: hardening

- ThreadSanitizer still clean (`scripts/tsan.sh`).
- Long-running soak test: scaling up and down, crash and restart recovery, no leaked VMs, containers or registered runners.
- Troubleshooting and security [known limits](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/security.md#known-limits) reviewed against what beta testers hit.
- Docs read-through against the shipped CLI and app.

**Exit:** no open data-loss, leaked-credential or leaked-runner bugs.

### v0.1.0: full release

- All the exit criteria above are met.
- Signed, notarized release with a working updater path from the last beta.
- Docs snapshot published under the version picker.

## How to help

Run kinhin on your own projects with a supported forge, then open a
[forge report](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/issues/new/choose) saying whether it worked.

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/support.md

# Support & sponsors

kinhin is free, Apache-2.0, and built by one developer, with no ads and no telemetry unless you opt in and point it at your own OpenTelemetry server ([Telemetry](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/telemetry.md)). Donations and sponsors pay for CI,
code signing, test hardware and development time.

[← Back to README](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/index.md)

## Support kinhin

| Where                                                                   | What                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/RabinApps)                | Monthly or one-time, with tiers   |
| [PayPal](https://www.paypal.com/donate/?hosted_button_id=YEJ37WF4Q3HPC) | One-time donation                 |
| [Buy Me a Coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/rabinapps)                   | One-time ($1 to $50+) or $1/month |

`kinhin support` prints the same links, and the menu bar app has **Support kinhin…** in its menu and Help menu.

## Become a sponsor

Companies can sponsor kinhin and have their logo and a link shown on the website's home page and in the app's
**Advanced → Settings** section. Pick a company tier on [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/RabinApps), or email
[support@rabinapps.com](mailto:support@rabinapps.com?subject=kinhin%20sponsorship) with your company name, link and
logo. Sponsorship supports the project; it does not buy influence over the roadmap.

## Sponsors

kinhin is sponsored by [SupDesk](https://supdesk.app), the feedback and support console for solo founders, devs and small
teams.

## Just using kinhin?

Add your project to [Who uses kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/used-by.md). It's free and takes one line.

## More from Rabin Apps

- [SupDesk](https://supdesk.app/en): the feedback and support console for solo founders, devs and small teams.

# Who uses kinhin

A short, hand-picked list of companies and projects that run their CI on kinhin. It appears on the website.

[← Back to README](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/index.md)

## Add your project

Open a pull request against `main` that adds one line to the `contributors` list in
[`website/.vitepress/sponsors.ts`](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/website/.vitepress/sponsors.ts):

```ts
{ sponsor: null, project: { name: "Your Project", url: "https://your-project.example", blurb: "What you build with kinhin." } },
```

- `name`: your project or company name.
- `url`: your own site.
- `blurb`: one short sentence about how you use kinhin.

A maintainer checks the link and the wording, then merges. The list updates with the next site build.

Want your logo shown instead? See [Support & sponsors](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/support.md#become-a-sponsor).

# CLI commands


```text
kinhin — autoscaling CI runners on your Mac.
Tart VMs run macOS jobs; apple/container, Docker or Tart Linux VMs run Linux jobs.
Forges: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Gitea, Forgejo (Buildkite, Azure, Bitbucket planned).

USAGE:
    kinhin                                  Setup status and the next step
    kinhin <command> [options]
    kinhin <command> --help                 Options for one command

SETUP:
    config init                             Write a starter config file
    config validate [FILE]                  Check the config without starting anything
    config reload                           Make the running daemon re-read the config
    config migrate                          Translate removed config keys to the current schema
    config export [FILE]                    Write the config for another Mac (no tokens)
    config import FILE                      Use a config exported on another Mac
    auth set                                Store (or replace) a token in the Keychain
    auth add NAME                           Add an account to the config
    auth list                               List accounts and whether their tokens are stored
    auth remove NAME                        Remove an account and delete its token
    auth status                             Check that stored tokens exist and work
    auth clear                              Remove a stored token
    doctor                                  Check prerequisites and the computed capacity
    setup status                            Show the first-run checklist
    setup repair host-agent                 Install the runner agents for host runs
    setup repair docker                     Install Docker
    setup repair container                  Install Apple container and its service
    setup repair tart                       Install tart for macOS VMs
    runtimes                                Pools, capacity, budget, health and routes
    runtimes route add <pattern> <runtime>  Route a repo or workflow to a runtime
    runtimes route remove <pattern>         Delete a route

IMAGES AND TOOLCHAINS:
    image prepare                           Build the runner base image (slow, once)
    image list                              Show installed images, their size and who uses them
    image delete <name>…                    Delete installed images by name
    image prune                             Sweep stale records and delete unused local images
    image digest <registry>/<repo>:<tag>    Print the digest a registry serves, to pin base_image
    toolchains                              Toolchain catalog, project selections and cache state
    toolchains detect [path]                Scan a checkout for the toolchains it needs
    toolchains list-images                  Derived per-project images: size and last used
    toolchains prune                        Expire stale cache entries and unused derived images
    toolchains helper                       Print the per-job kinhin-toolchain helper script
    mobile                                  Set up fastlane store releases for a mobile app
    mobile init [DIR]                       Add fastlane lanes and the CI release workflow

RUNNING:
    start                                   Start the fleet in this terminal (Ctrl-C to stop)
    daemon                                  Run the headless daemon in this terminal
    daemon install                          Install and start a LaunchAgent daemon
    daemon uninstall                        Stop and remove the LaunchAgent
    status                                  Show fleet status (attaches to the daemon)
    pause                                   Hold the fleet: no new runners start
    resume                                  Let a paused fleet scale again
    stop                                    Stop the fleet (works on a daemon)
    logs                                    Show recent log lines
    watch                                   Live status view (refreshes every 2s)
    pipeline [VM]                           Live jobs and steps of the VMs that are busy
    requeue <forge>                         Re-queue the fleet's queued jobs on a forge
    skip <forge>                            Mark the fleet's queued jobs as skipped on a forge
    heal                                    What the healing agent fixed, and what waits on you
    heal approve ID                         Carry out a fix that waits for approval
    heal dismiss ID                         Close a pending or surfaced entry
    telemetry                               OpenTelemetry export: what runs and what fails
    cleanup                                 Reclaim disk: leftover VMs, the base image, the cache
    bench [SUITE]…                          Benchmark runtimes, workloads and toolchains here
    reset                                   Reset config, the daemon install, or everything

WORKFLOWS:
    workflow test [FILE]                    Run a workflow locally on this Mac (host execution)
    workflow route <FILE|name> <runtime>    Route a workflow's jobs to a runtime

OTHER:
    video init [name]                       Create a starter video in .kinhin/videos/
    video list                              List the videos in .kinhin/videos/
    video build [name]                      Build a video from its config
    video validate [name]                   Check a video's config without rendering it
    video theme list                        List the built-in themes and yours
    video theme new <name>                  Write a starter theme file
    video record <app or title>             Record one app window as a clip, without the mouse
                                            pointer
    video music search <words>              Search openly licensed music
    video music preview <number|id>         Listen to a search result
    video music add <number|id|name>        Download a track into the repository and use it
    video music list                        Show the music each video uses
    support                                 Show ways to donate or sponsor kinhin
    issue                                   Submit an issue on GitHub
    mcp                                     Serve MCP over stdio for AI agents
    version                                 Print the version
    help [command]                          Show this help, or `help <command>` for one command

EXIT CODES:
    0 ok    1 needs attention    2 usage error    3 config    4 runtime    5 auth

Add --json for machine-readable output. Docs: https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/tree/main/docs
```

## Exit codes

Scripts can branch on the exit code.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Needs attention (not healthy), or anything unclassified |
| 2 | Bad command line |
| 3 | Invalid or unreadable config |
| 4 | Runtime or engine failure |
| 5 | Missing or rejected token |
| 130 | Cancelled (Ctrl-C); in-progress work was cleaned up |

## How scaling works

Every `poll_interval` seconds the engine:

1. Cleans up any failed instances from the previous pass.
2. Asks each forge for queued jobs on its scope and filters them by `labels`.
3. **Routes** each job to a runtime — workflow route → repo route → `runs-on:` label → default —
   and buckets the demand per pool.
4. Computes the desired instance count **per pool**:
   `desired = clamp(ceil(pool_queue / runners_per_vm), min_runners, pool_cap)`.
5. Spawns instances up to `desired` (linked clone → boot → SSH → register `runners_per_vm`
   runners → `run.sh`) — Tart VMs for macOS and Tart-Linux pools, containers for the container
   Linux pools (see [Runtimes & routing](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/runtimes.md#choosing-a-linux-runtime)).
6. Deletes idle instances when `desired` drops (scale to zero by default).

Runners register `--ephemeral`, so the forge removes the registration as soon as the job
finishes; kinhin then deletes the VM. If the engine crashes or restarts it reconciles
`tart list` against its persisted state, adopts orphaned VMs, and drops records whose VMs
vanished.

Registration tokens are short-lived (1 h); kinhin caches and refreshes them automatically.
Your PAT lives in the login Keychain.

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/agents.md

# Use kinhin from AI agents

Two ways AI agents meet kinhin: **operating a fleet** on someone's Mac, and **contributing to the kinhin
repository** itself. Both surfaces are deliberate: every read command has a machine-readable document, the CLI
speaks MCP, and the skills under [`skills/`](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/tree/main/skills) teach an agent
the workflows around the commands.

## Skills

Eight skills ship in the repository — one per workflow an agent actually performs:

| Skill | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `kinhin-install` | Install kinhin and Tart, first-time setup, a rented or remote Mac |
| `kinhin-configure` | Write `config.yaml` safely: accounts, labels, capacity, routes |
| `kinhin-operate` | Start/stop/pause, status, logs, pipeline view, daemon, cleanup, scaling |
| `kinhin-add-forge-account` | Connect a GitHub, GitLab, Gitea or Forgejo account |
| `kinhin-images-toolchains` | `image prepare`, base-image pinning, `.kinhin/config.yml`, per-project toolchains |
| `kinhin-route-workflow` | Choose and route a workflow to tart, appleContainer, docker or host |
| `kinhin-troubleshoot` | Jobs queued but no VMs, registration failures, token rejected, disk filling |
| `kinhin-video` | Make a narrated product video from `.kinhin/videos/`: scenes, themes, captions, CC0 music search, container or fleet builds |

Each skill's frontmatter `description:` is what your agent's matcher reads, and every command inside it is checked
against `kinhin help` by `scripts/skills-lint.sh` — a skill cannot outlive a renamed command.

**Any agent** — the open [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installer reads `skills/*/SKILL.md`
straight from the repository and copies or links them into each agent's skills directory:

```sh
npx skills add RabinApps/kinhin --skill '*' --global      # every skill, user-wide
npx skills add RabinApps/kinhin --list                     # see them first
npx skills add RabinApps/kinhin --skill kinhin-install --agent claude-code --yes
npx skills update                                          # later: pull new versions
```

**Claude Code, as a plugin** — the repository is also a plugin marketplace:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add RabinApps/kinhin
claude plugin install kinhin@kinhin
```

Or copy the `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` files by hand (Claude-format frontmatter is the de-facto standard).

## MCP: `kinhin mcp`

`kinhin mcp` is an MCP server on stdio: JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line, stdout carrying protocol only. It
exposes the CLI's non-printing cores, so a tool answer is byte-identical to the command's `--json` document.

```sh
claude mcp add kinhin -- kinhin mcp     # Claude Code
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kinhin": { "command": "kinhin", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
```

| Tool | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | The `kinhin status --json` document: daemon reachability, running/paused, queue depth |
| `doctor` | Prerequisites, tokens, runtime health, the capacity cap, image disk usage (`imageTotalGB`), prune hint (`imagePrune`) and the disk-pressure warning (`diskPressure`) — `kinhin doctor --json` (offline; add `--check-tokens` for live per-account token verdicts under `tokenChecks`) |
| `setup_status` | The first-run checklist and its `ready` flag |
| `runtimes` | Pools, budget split, health, routes (`noHealth: true` skips probes) |
| `auth_status` | Which forges have a stored token — never the token itself |
| `pipeline` | The live jobs and steps a busy VM runs (needs the daemon; `vm`, `job` filters) |
| `logs` | The log file's tail, redacted for tokens (`limit` caps it) |
| `heal_status` | The healing agent's journal, the `kinhin heal --json` document: fixes it ran, fixes waiting for approval, problems only the user can fix ([details](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/healing.md)). Read-only |
| `pause` / `resume` / `stop` | Fleet control through the daemon, with a `message` result |
| `daemon_install` | Install and start the headless LaunchAgent |

**Deliberately not exposed**: `reset`, `cleanup --yes`, `auth set`, `heal approve` / `heal dismiss`, and everything that blocks (`start`,
`watch`). The server's `initialize` response carries the same rule as `instructions`, so an agent that never
reads the docs still learns the boundary. A failed tool call answers `isError: true` in-band; protocol errors
are reserved for malformed requests.

## The `--json` CLI surface

For agents that shell out instead of speaking MCP:

- **stdout carries only the document.** Notes and warnings go to stderr, so a redirect or pipe is always
  parseable. Documents are pretty-printed with sorted keys.
- **Exit codes classify the failure**: `0` success, `1` general, `2` usage, `3` config, `4` runtime/engine,
  `5` auth, `130` cancelled (Ctrl-C).
- Two commands use exit `1` as "not ready yet": `kinhin auth status --json` and `kinhin setup status` exit 1
  until setup is complete (`doctor --json` reports `ready=false` instead of failing). `kinhin heal` exits 1 while a
  fix waits for approval or a problem needs the user, and when no daemon runs.

| Command | Document |
| --- | --- |
| `kinhin status --json` | Fleet status, flattened `paused` / `autoResume` / `queueAgeSeconds` fields |
| `kinhin doctor --json` | Merged diagnostics: host, runtimes, tokens, checklist, capacity, image disk usage (`imageTotalGB`), prune hint (`imagePrune`), disk pressure (`diskPressure`) |
| `kinhin setup status --json` | First-run checklist |
| `kinhin auth status --json` | Stored-token state across every configured forge, or one account with `--account NAME` |
| `kinhin auth list --json` | Every account with its scope and token state (`stored`, `none`, `error`); never the token |
| `kinhin runtimes [--json] [--no-health]` | Pools, capacity, budget, health, routes |
| `kinhin pipeline [VM] [--job N] --json` | Live jobs and steps |
| `kinhin config validate --json` | `valid` + parsed facts, or `valid: false` + `error` (exit 3) |
| `kinhin cleanup … --json` | Dry-run report: what a cleanup *would* remove; refuses `--yes` |
| `kinhin workflow test … --json` | Local workflow-run report with `outcome` (`succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`, …); exit 1 unless `succeeded` (`--lenient` also accepts `partial`) |
| `kinhin workflow route … --json` | What the route edit did or would do |
| `kinhin toolchains detect … --json` | Detected toolchains and the evidence, with `--write` to save |
| `kinhin bench … --json` | The benchmark report (see [Benchmarks](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/benchmarks.md)); pauses a running fleet and takes minutes, so ask first (needs `--yes` with a live fleet outside a terminal); exit 1 when a suite or toolchain row failed |
| `kinhin image list --json [--runtime <name>]` | Installed images per runtime: name, role, size, last used, who uses them |
| `kinhin heal --json` | The healing journal: `pending` fixes, `surfaced` problems and every event, newest first ([fields](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/healing.md#the-json-document)) |

## Safety rules for agents

- **Never run `kinhin reset`.** There is no undo and no backup.
- **Ask before `kinhin cleanup --yes`, `kinhin image delete --yes`, `kinhin image prune --yes`, `kinhin stop` or
  `kinhin daemon uninstall`** on a fleet that may be serving jobs; `kinhin cleanup --json` and
  `kinhin image list --json` are the safe ways to show a human what would go first (plain `kinhin image prune` is the
  same report without the deletion). `kinhin stop` reaches the daemon install only — when the menu bar app runs the
  fleet in-process, stopping the fleet means asking the human to stop it in the app.
- **Ask before `kinhin bench`** on a fleet that may be serving jobs: it pauses the fleet while it measures and creates
  temporary VMs. Pass `--yes` only once the user has agreed to that; never pass `--include-host` unasked.
- **Host routes are unisolated** — `runtimes route add <pattern> host` requires `--consent` and runs repo code
  directly on the Mac. Don't add one without the user asking.
- **Never approve or dismiss a healing fix for the user.** `kinhin heal approve` can prune images or reinstall a
  runtime. Show the entry from `kinhin heal --json` (or `heal_status`) and let the user run `kinhin heal approve ID`
  themselves. The same goes for the fixes the journal lists as theirs, such as a new token.
- **Tokens never appear in any document.** `auth status --json` reports presence and validity only.
- `requeue` and `skip` confirm interactively; pass `--yes` only when the user asked for exactly that.

Agents contributing code should start at [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/AGENTS.md)
(or `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code): both point at `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the one-shot gate
`scripts/check.sh`.
