**Be careful, whatever you use, if** the code you run is not yours. A VM boundary is real isolation. Docker is weaker (a
shared kernel and default capabilities). Host mode has no isolation at all. The shared toolchain cache is writable and
trusted by later jobs, so it defaults to off. If you run fork PRs or outside contributors' code, turn on the settings in
the [security guide](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/security.md#if-you-run-untrusted-prs-turn-these-on) first and read the
[known limits](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/security.md#known-limits). For a public repository, the
[open-source guide](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/open-source.md) shows how to keep fork pull requests off your Mac entirely.

### Try it

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

The installer verifies a signed, notarized DMG, installs `kinhin.app` and links the `kinhin` CLI.

You need an Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 15 or newer with about 60 GB of free disk, and an access token for your forge. The
[Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md) goes from install to a running fleet, and [Hardware and sizing](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/hardware.md) helps
you decide how big a Mac you need.

## What has been tested, and what has not

I use two words precisely:

- **Live-tested** means it was run against a real server, with a real workflow job, on a real Mac.
- **Unit-tested only** means automated tests against fakes, stubbed HTTP and fake shells, and **never run against a real
  instance**. Those tests show the code matches my reading of an API, not that the real service agrees. Buildkite, Azure
  Pipelines and Bitbucket Pipelines are at this stage, which is why they are not supported yet.

| Area                                                                                                           | State at beta-1                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| GitHub Actions + Tart macOS VMs, apple/container                                                               | Live-tested, by hand                      |
| Gitea (1.24, 1.26), Forgejo 11, GitLab CE 18.4 on Tart macOS and Linux VMs, apple/container, Docker, host mode | Live-tested, by the end-to-end suite      |
| Crash recovery, concurrency cap, pause and resume, forge outages, warm pool, routing                           | Live-tested, by the end-to-end suite      |
| Toolchain installs (baked and per job)                                                                         | Live-tested, by the end-to-end suite      |
| Buildkite, Azure Pipelines, Bitbucket Pipelines                                                                | Planned, not supported yet                |
| In-app updater against a published release                                                                     | Not exercised (this is the first release) |
| ThreadSanitizer                                                                                                | One clean run of `scripts/tsan.sh`        |
| Long-running soak test                                                                                         | Not done                                  |

There are about 2,900 unit tests that need no VMs or network. They run in about two minutes, and they are not evidence that
the real services agree with me.

Measured once on my own Mac (M1 Max, 64 GB, macOS 27) with `kinhin bench`: a Tart macOS VM boots to SSH-ready in about
31 s cold and 10 s warm, an apple/container Linux container is ready in about 1.4 s, and `xcodebuild` builds a small
generated Swift package inside the VM in 13 s clean and 3.5 s incremental. One machine, one run: treat these as a sample,
not a benchmark.

### The end-to-end suite

"Live-tested" is not me, by hand, once. An automated end-to-end suite (`scripts/e2e.sh`, described in the
[e2e docs](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/docs/e2e-testing.md)) starts a real Gitea, Forgejo or GitLab CE
in a container, runs a real kinhin daemon against it in a sandbox that cannot touch my own setup, bakes a real runner
image, pushes a workflow, and then checks what the forge itself reports: the job ran inside the guest (it files an issue
containing the guest's kernel and hostname), the instance was deleted afterwards, the runner was deregistered, and no
token reached the log. It runs Gitea, Forgejo and GitLab CE on every runtime, plus failing jobs, long jobs, a daemon killed mid-run, a
forge that hangs mid-job, the concurrency cap, the warm pool, routing, and toolchain installs. The GitHub lane needs a
throwaway repository and a token, so GitHub's live runs are still my own.

## How this was built

Because agents type the code, the checks carry the weight. Every change has to pass `scripts/check.sh` (build, the unit suite, format, docs and skills lint), the e2e suite is the part that runs real software rather than fakes, and anything that touches shared state also gets a ThreadSanitizer run. `scripts/check.sh` is green on the release commit. Weigh all of that however you like — it's also why the testing table above is as blunt as it is.

## Where I need help

I have one Mac, one GitHub setup, and a finite supply of evenings. The fastest way to improve this beta is to run the parts
I could not. In rough order of value:

1. **Real projects on the supported forges.** Your workflows, not my test jobs: GitHub, Gitea, Forgejo and GitLab CE.
2. **Other versions:** newer Forgejo, Gitea 1.25, older GitLab CE releases.
3. **GitHub on Docker and host mode**, and Docker through OrbStack or colima. I have used Docker Desktop.
4. **Mixed fleets:** more than one account or forge sharing one pool, and mixed runtimes routed by label.
5. **Different hardware:** other Mac sizes and macOS versions, especially 8 GB and 16 GB machines.
6. **The updater**, once a later release is published.
7. **Docs and first run.** If you got stuck, that is a bug in the docs or the app.

One real job is a valuable report, including when it fails.

### How to report

Open a [forge or runtime report](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/issues/new/choose) and say whether it worked end to
end, partly, or failed, what you ran, and what went wrong. Attach the output of:

```bash
kinhin doctor --bundle
```

It writes a redacted bundle (doctor report, config and recent log). Tokens are masked, but please glance through it before
attaching. A good report names the forge and its version, the runtime, and the first thing that went wrong. Here is what
happens to it: I reproduce it, fix it, add a test, and once a forge or runtime has passed a real run the table above and
the docs change to say so.

## Contributing

Bug reports, feature requests and pull requests are welcome, including AI-assisted ones. The repository has an
[`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and a `CLAUDE.md` that point agents at the rules.
The short version: follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/contributing.md) exactly, run `scripts/check.sh` before opening a PR, keep
mechanical changes in separate commits, and own the change whether a human or a model typed it. You can also
[add your project to "Who uses kinhin"](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/used-by.md) or [support the project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/support.md).

## Goals

The goal of this beta is narrow: make the four supported forges solid on real projects, then add the next ones. The
milestones are ordered by what has to be true, not by date; the complete version is the
[beta roadmap](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/beta-roadmap.md).

- **beta-2: hardening the supported forges.** Fixes from beta testers, the updater exercised against a published release,
  and the e2e suite running nightly on a dedicated Mac.
- **beta-3: more forges.** Buildkite, Azure Pipelines and Bitbucket Pipelines, each supported once it passes the same
  end-to-end runs. Mixed-forge fleets.
- **Release candidate: hardening.** ThreadSanitizer still clean, a long soak test with no leaked VMs, containers or
  registered runners, and the known limits reviewed against what testers hit.
- **v0.1.0.** A signed, notarized release with a working updater path, and a docs snapshot under the version picker.

## Windows

Windows runners are not part of the beta and I'm not promising them for v0.1.0. Windows containers aren't possible on this
stack, which leaves Windows on ARM virtual machines, a new runtime with its own VM lifecycle, guest access, images and
runner install per forge. There is a design sketch in the repository, and the hypervisor options are constrained and, in the
Parallels case, need a paid license and install media. If Windows matters to you, open an issue describing your forge,
concurrency and hypervisor. It won't be called supported until it has run for real.

## Principles

The principles stay fixed: jobs are ephemeral by default, the scaler never starves your Mac, credentials stay in the
Keychain, there is no telemetry, and one engine serves every forge.

## Thank you

kinhin is free, Apache-2.0, and built by one developer with AI agents. If it saves you CI minutes you can
[support it](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/support.md) through GitHub Sponsors, PayPal or Buy Me a Coffee. Sponsorship supports the project and does
not buy influence over the roadmap.

- [Install and Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md)
- [What has been tested](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md#what-has-been-tested) and the [beta roadmap](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/beta-roadmap.md)
- [kinhin on GitHub](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin) and the [issue templates](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/issues/new/choose)

And if a job runs on your Mac and you didn't have to babysit it, that's the whole point.

_Alex_

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/blog/beta-4.md

# Beta 4: telemetry you opt into, macOS 27 images, and fixes from your installs

_Friday, October 30, 2026 · Alex Rabin_

<figure>
  <video controls playsinline preload="metadata" :poster="'/beta-4-poster.png'" style="width: 100%; border-radius: 8px">
    <source :src="'/beta-4.webm'" type="video/webm" />
    <source :src="'/beta-4.mp4'" type="video/mp4" />
    <a href="/beta-4.mp4">Watch the beta 4 video</a>
  </video>
</figure>

**kinhin** watches your CI queue and, for each queued job, starts a fresh VM or container on your Apple Silicon Mac,
registers a one-job runner, lets it run, then deletes it. Nothing idles and nothing is left over. It is free, open source
(Apache-2.0), and sends no telemetry unless you point it at your own OpenTelemetry server.

Beta 4 adds that opt-in telemetry, the macOS 27 base images, and a round of fixes for problems people hit when they installed
beta 3. It also has one breaking change for Linux runners. This post covers what is new, what to do when you upgrade, what has
been run, and what has not.

## What is new

### Telemetry you opt into

kinhin can now export metrics, traces and logs about the fleet and the jobs it runs. It is **off by default**. Until you set
`telemetry.enabled: true`, kinhin starts no exporter, opens no port and sends nothing anywhere. When you turn it on, the data
goes to a collector you run, such as Grafana Alloy or the OpenTelemetry Collector. It never goes to me.

- Metrics cover workers by pool and state, queue depth and age, fleet size, the warm pool, boot and registration timings, jobs
  picked up and completed, forge request counts and rate limits, and classified errors. No VM, job or run ID is a metric label.
- Each instance gets one trace. The job result and step spans come from the forge when it can say, and read `unknown` otherwise.
- Logs go over OTLP too, and `log_format: json` writes structured local logs.
- `prometheus_listen` serves the metrics on a local Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint, bound to `127.0.0.1` unless you say otherwise.
- `kinhin telemetry status` shows what the daemon sends where, and whether exports are failing.
- `kinhin config reload` makes the running daemon re-read your config. Telemetry and routing changes apply in place, and an
  invalid file is refused before it reaches the daemon.
- The app has a Telemetry card under Advanced → App that shows the export status and switches it on or off.
- A Grafana dashboard and alert rules are in the repository, with a ready Alloy snippet.

Two honest limits. The OpenTelemetry Swift SDK marks traces stable, but metrics and logs as still in development upstream, so
**treat this as beta** and expect a rough edge there. And passing trace context into your workflow steps is not part of this
release. Setup, the metric list and the privacy notes are in the [telemetry guide](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/docs/telemetry.md).

This is covered by unit tests and the end-to-end cases written for it. I have not yet exported from a live fleet to a real
collector, so the dashboard and the alert rules are untested against real data.

### macOS 27 base images

The macOS 27 "Golden Gate" images (`macos-golden-gate-base`, `-vanilla` and `-xcode`) are in the base-image picker. A
`ghcr.io/cirruslabs/macos-*` reference pinned by `@sha256:` is accepted too, because the pin names exact bits and stays
servable after its tag is retired. When kinhin refuses a base image, it now says what it would accept, including
`kinhin image digest` for printing a pin. See [Choosing the base image](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/docs/runtimes.md#choosing-the-base-image).
I have not yet booted a Golden Gate image and run a job on it. The picker and the digest handling are covered by unit tests.

### Fixes from install feedback

- **`kinhin daemon install`** wrote whatever path it was run by into the LaunchAgent. A bare `kinhin` resolved through `PATH`
  became `<cwd>/kinhin`, which launchd could not run at login. The path now comes from the running binary, and the install checks
  that the agent actually started. A daemon that exits at once is reported as a failure.
- **`warm_pool: 1`** could keep two VMs, because a pooled VM still cloning or booting was invisible to the scale plan. In-flight
  pooled VMs now count toward the target and the caps.
- **`vm.cpu` and `vm.memory_gb`** were ignored on Tart. They are now set on the clone before its first boot, and a failed
  `tart set` fails the spawn instead of booting an unconstrained VM.
- **`image delete` and `image prune`** stopped at the first image that could not be deleted. They now continue, report every
  failure at the end, and keep the record of an image that failed so you can try again.
- **The budget bar** in `kinhin runtimes` printed only edge values, because it rounded at the wrong step.
- **Multi-runner VMs** show every running job in the fleet view, not just one.
- **Timers** no longer keep ticking on a finished job.

There is also `kinhin config validate FILE`, which checks a named file instead of this Mac's default config. It helps before you
point a fleet at a file, and in CI.

## Upgrading

**This is a breaking change.** Apple-container and Docker runners no longer advertise the `macos` label. Their guests run Linux,
and a macOS job started there would never finish. If a workflow has `runs-on: […, macos]` and means a Linux runtime, change it
to the marker label: `kinhin-container` or `kinhin-docker`. If a Linux pool should not inherit the fleet's labels at all, set
`fleet_labels: false` under `container:` or `docker:`. The pool then registers with the marker
and that section's own labels alone. [Runtimes](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/docs/runtimes.md) has the details.

Also:

- If the daemon does not start after the upgrade, re-run `kinhin daemon install`.
- The default `image:` can now carry runner labels through `image_labels:`. A Linux default base keeps macOS jobs off its runners.
- **The updater.** Beta 3 introduced in-app updates through Sparkle, and beta 3 to beta 4 is the first time a published release
  updates a published release. When the app restarts the daemon onto the new build, **it interrupts that daemon's running jobs**,
  so update when the fleet is idle.
I have not yet watched a real beta 3 install this update itself. If it fails, install over it by hand and tell me.

## What has been run

**Run** means it was executed for this release. **Not yet** means it has not been, and I am not claiming it.

- **Run:** the unit suite (no VMs or network) and the repository's release checks, locally on the release preparation commit. One Docker-engine test failed once under the parallel run and passed on the rerun and on its own, so I count it as a flaky test, not a fix.
- **Not yet:** ThreadSanitizer on the release commit.
- **Not yet:** an upgrade from beta 3 with real state, and the daemon starting at login from the new LaunchAgent path.
- **Not yet:** a live job on a Linux runner under the new labels. The label rules are covered by unit tests.
- **Not yet:** `vm.cpu`, `vm.memory_gb` and `warm_pool: 1` on a live Tart host. They are covered by unit tests.
- **Not yet:** the end-to-end suite on this release. It runs only in CI, and its dedicated Mac is not registered yet.
- **Not yet:** the Buildkite, Azure Pipelines and Bitbucket Pipelines lanes. Azure stays experimental, Buildkite and
  Bitbucket stay planned, and GitHub, Gitea, Forgejo and GitLab CE remain the supported forges.
- **Not yet:** a long-running soak test.

## Try it

The release is published on [GitHub](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/releases/tag/v0.0.1-beta-4). Install it with:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

You need an Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 15 or newer with about 60 GB of free disk, and an access token for your forge. The
[Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md) goes from install to a running fleet. Coming from beta 3, the app can update itself, or you
can install over it when no jobs are running.

## Where I need help

1. **The first real in-app update.** Update from beta 3 to beta 4 in the app and tell me whether it downloaded, installed and
   relaunched.
2. **Telemetry on a real collector.** Point it at yours, import the dashboard, load the alert rules, and tell me what is wrong
   or missing. Send the output of `kinhin telemetry status` if exports fail.
3. **The label change.** Move a Linux workflow to `kinhin-container` or `kinhin-docker` and tell me whether anything still
   lands on the wrong runner.
4. **A fresh install.** Run `kinhin daemon install` from a clean shell and reboot. Tell me whether the daemon came back.
5. **macOS 27 images.** Tell me what you build on Golden Gate and what breaks.
6. **Real projects on the supported forges, and real Azure DevOps builds.**

One real report is valuable, including when it fails. Open a
[forge or runtime report](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/issues/new/choose) and attach the output of
`kinhin doctor --bundle` after a glance through it, since it is redacted but not perfect.

## Thank you

Thank you for installing the betas and reporting what you find. kinhin is free and Apache-2.0. If it saves you CI minutes, you
can [support it](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/support.md).

_Alex_

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/blog/beta-3.md

# Beta 3: updates that install themselves, restarts that leave your jobs alone, and seven new languages

_Saturday, October 24, 2026 · Alex Rabin_

**kinhin** watches your CI queue and, for each queued job, starts a fresh VM or container on your Apple Silicon Mac,
registers a one-job runner, lets it run, then deletes it. Nothing idles and nothing is left over. It is free, open source
(Apache-2.0), and sends no telemetry.

Beta 3 keeps a promise from the beta 2 post, makes the app update itself, and adds a few things for people who make videos
or run their own models. This post covers what is new, what has been run, and what has not.

## Keeping a promise: restarts

The beta 2 post carried a correction: on beta 2, restarting kinhin re-attached running VMs and then registered their runners
again, which could disrupt a job already running on one. Beta 3 fixes that.

- A restart no longer registers a VM again while its runner is still on the forge. A runner the forge still has is watched. A VM
  with no runner is registered as normal.
- A VM whose forge cannot be asked is held, shown by an `adoption` alert, until it can be. A VM whose account has no forge
  attached is held the same way and removed after one hour. A VM whose account was removed from the config is released at once.
- A classic container runner is registered again after a host reboot or `container system stop`, when the forge no longer has it.
- Registration stops a leftover agent without `pkill`, and fails if it survives.

[Restarts](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/docs/scaling.md#restarts) explains each rule.
I tested this live on 2026-10-24: I upgraded a Mac with real state from beta 2, and restarted kinhin while a job was running. The job was left alone.

## What is new

### An updater that installs itself

The app now updates through [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org). It downloads the new release, checks its EdDSA signature,
replaces the running app and relaunches. It checks once a day, and Settings → App shows **Install Update…** when one is
waiting. After an upgrade, the app restarts a daemon still running the previous build, which **interrupts that daemon's jobs**,
so update when the fleet is idle.

Beta 2 and earlier open the DMG for a manual drag into Applications, and beta 2 published no update feed, so you update by hand
**once**, from beta 2 to beta 3. Updates after that install automatically.
The in-app install has not been exercised against a published release yet. That needs a release that already contains the
updater, so the first real test is beta 3 to the next release.

### Healing with your own models

The healing agent can ask [Ollama](https://ollama.com) instead of Apple Intelligence: `healing: {ai: ollama, ollama: {model: …}}`.
An optional `fast_model` is asked first, and the larger model answers when it is not confident. Traffic goes to this Mac by
default. Any other host must be `https`, and it then receives the redacted problem, the allowed fixes and the log lines. It still only chooses among
fixes that are already allowed. See [docs/healing.md](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/docs/healing.md#the-ollama-advisor).

### Videos with a camera

Videos from your repository got a director:

- A `device` or `terminal` scene's `camera` zooms and pans, `focus` spotlights part of the screen and `cursor` adds a pointer with
  click rings. Adapters can name regions of a clip, so a redesigned screen is fixed once.
- `karaoke` captions light each word as it is spoken. `transition` replaces the fade between scenes. `speed` takes eased
  segments, and a `split` scene plays two recordings side by side.
- Rebuilds reuse the voice and the framed clips, so a one-line edit no longer redoes the video. `kinhin video build --scene app,outro`
  builds a quick preview, `--watch` rebuilds on change, and every build prints how long each step took.

Nothing changes for a video that does not use them.

### Seven new languages for the app

The menu bar app now follows the macOS language in Spanish, Japanese, German, Hebrew, Arabic, Italian and French. **These are
first drafts, not reviewed by native speakers.** The CLI, its output and the docs stay English. Disclosure arrows mirror in
right-to-left languages.
I have not looked at every language in the running app, so expect truncated text or odd layout somewhere.

### Fixes

- `kinhin image digest` and the app's Pin button no longer fail with `registry answered HTTP 404` for Cirrus Labs images.
- A new VM no longer waits the whole `vm_boot_timeout` when macOS Local Network privacy blocks its port 22 probe. After 15
  seconds kinhin tries SSH anyway and logs why. The app declares a Local Network usage description.
- `kinhin doctor` no longer calls Command Line Tools outdated when they only trail macOS by a patch release.
- `kinhin auth list --json` exists, and `kinhin auth status --account NAME --json` reports only that account.
- Azure DevOps warns at start-up when the agent pool has no matching agent.

## Where the forges stand

Beta 3 was going to be the "more forges" release. It is not. Buildkite, Azure Pipelines and Bitbucket Pipelines need real
accounts and a dedicated test Mac that I have not set up, and I would rather ship what is done than claim support I have not
run. **Azure Pipelines is now labelled experimental**: one user ran smoke jobs against Azure DevOps Services, two concurrent
VMs and scale from zero, but not a real application build. **Buildkite and Bitbucket Pipelines are still planned.** Test fixtures for
all three are written and have not run. This work moves to beta 4. GitHub, Gitea, Forgejo and GitLab CE remain the supported
forges.

## What has been run

**Run** means it was executed for this release. **Not yet** means it has not been, and I am not claiming it.

- **Run:** the unit suite (3,453 tests, no VMs or network) and the release build's own check, on the release commit.
- **Run:** the ThreadSanitizer run on the release commit, with no reports.
- **Run:** an upgrade from beta 2 on a Mac with real state (nothing lost), and a restart under a real running job, which was left alone. One Mac, one pass.
- **Not yet:** the end-to-end suite on this release. It runs only in CI, and its dedicated Mac is not registered yet.
- **Not yet:** the Buildkite, Azure Pipelines and Bitbucket Pipelines lanes.
- **Not yet:** a long-running soak test.

## Try it

The release is published on [GitHub](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/releases/tag/v0.0.1-beta-3). Install it with:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

You need an Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 15 or newer with about 60 GB of free disk, and an access token for your forge. The
[Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md) goes from install to a running fleet. Coming from beta 2, install over it by hand once, when no
jobs are running.

## Where I need help

1. **Restarting under load.** Restart the daemon (or reboot the Mac) while jobs run, and tell me whether any job was disturbed.
2. **Upgrading with real state.** Your fleet, project images and config, on beta 2, then beta 3. Tell me if anything was lost.
3. **The updater.** The first in-app update is from this release to the next. Tell me whether it installed and relaunched.
4. **A language that is not English.** Tell me which strings are wrong, awkward or cut off.
5. **Ollama healing and video cameras.** Send me a journal entry or a video that looks wrong.
6. **Real projects on the supported forges, and real Azure DevOps builds.**

One real report is valuable, including when it fails. Open a
[forge or runtime report](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/issues/new/choose) and attach the output of
`kinhin doctor --bundle` after a glance through it, since it is redacted but not perfect.

## Thank you

kinhin is free and Apache-2.0. If it saves you CI minutes, you can [support it](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/support.md).

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/blog/beta-2.md

# Beta 2: a fleet that heals itself, warm pools per image, and videos from your repo

_Friday, October 16, 2026 · Alex Rabin_

**kinhin** watches your CI queue and, for each queued job, starts a fresh VM or container on your Apple Silicon Mac,
registers a one-job runner, lets it run, then deletes it. Nothing idles and nothing is left over. It is free, open source
(Apache-2.0), and sends no telemetry.

Beta 2 is the release where the fleet looks after itself a little, the warm pools get finer-grained, and your repository can
make its own launch videos. This post covers what is new, what has been run, and what has not.

## What is new

### A fleet that heals itself

Fleets break in dull ways: a warm VM gets deleted outside kinhin, a toolchain cache fills the disk, an account gets detached,
or the Apple container system stops. The healing agent now fixes four of those on its own: a warm VM deleted out of band, a
toolchain cache filling the disk, a detached account, and a stopped Apple container system.

Anything destructive waits for you. Pruning images or reinstalling a runtime goes into a journal:

- `kinhin heal` shows the journal.
- `kinhin heal approve ID` carries out a fix you have reviewed. `kinhin heal dismiss ID` closes an entry.
- The app's Diagnostics sheet has a Healing card, and a notification fires when a fix succeeds.
- It is configured under `healing:`. [docs/healing.md](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/docs/healing.md)
  describes each rule.

On macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence turned on, the on-device model can choose from the allowed fixes for a problem that no
rule covers. It only chooses among fixes that are already allowed.

### Warm pools per image

A warm pool keeps booted, unregistered VMs ready, so the next job skips the clone and the boot. Until now the pool covered
only the top-level `image:`. Beta 2 adds `warm_pool` on any `images:` entry, so a job routed to a named image such as `xcode`
gets a ready VM too. The top-level `warm_pool` still covers `image:`, and the two share `max_runners`.

Each image in the app's **More images** card has a stepper for its pool, and the Capacity view shows the base image's. Changes
are saved once the stepper settles.

A warm VM costs RAM and disk, and it holds a `max_runners` slot while it waits. Turning a pool off, or removing an `images:`
entry, recycles its VMs straight away.

### Videos from your repository

`kinhin video` makes a narrated video of your own product from `.kinhin/videos/*.yml`. You do not copy the video suite into
your repository: the build runs a published container image (Apple `container` or Docker) against your files.

- `kinhin video init`, `list` and `build` cover the basics. Each build lands in its own folder under `.kinhin/videos/out/`.
- Music, captions, themes and formats are config. `kinhin video theme new` starts a theme that extends a built-in one.
- `kinhin video music search` finds CC0 and public-domain tracks. `--license cc-by` also offers CC BY tracks and writes the
  credit line.
- `--on-fleet` builds on a runner through a generated GitHub workflow.
- The app's Fleet tab has a **Make a Video…** sheet that uses the same code, with live output.
- A `device` scene can show store screenshots as a cross-fading slideshow.

### Recording a clip of your app

`kinhin video record <app or title>` records one window of an app as a clip, with the mouse pointer left out. `--list-windows`
shows what can be recorded, and `--window ID` picks one. The first run needs Screen Recording permission for your terminal,
which you grant once in System Settings.

### Mobile releases and store screenshots

`kinhin mobile init` scaffolds release setup for iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native, native projects, Capacitor and Ionic,
Kotlin Multiplatform and .NET MAUI, with lanes, a pinned Gemfile and a manual `mobile-release` workflow for `kinhin-xcode`.
Expo gets EAS config. It is opt-in: a project that does not run it sees no change.

A `screenshots` lane captures iOS UI tests with `snapshot` and Android instrumented tests with `screengrab`, with optional
device frames and upload.

`--ci` writes a pipeline for GitLab CI, Gitea and Forgejo Actions, Bitbucket Pipelines, Azure Pipelines or Buildkite as well
as GitHub Actions. Those files run your mobile release on that system. kinhin does not scale runners for Buildkite, Azure
Pipelines or Bitbucket Pipelines yet, which is beta-3 work. Treat the generated pipelines as untested on your project until a
run of your own has passed.

### Fleet safety and fixes

- An unreadable `fleet.json`, `project-images.json` or scale-set session file is moved aside to `<name>.corrupt-<timestamp>`
  instead of being replaced. kinhin starts empty, and the app and `kinhin status` name the kept copy.
  > **Correction:** "starts empty" was unclear and understated the risk. kinhin starts with no VM records, but on beta 2 it re-attaches
  > the VMs still running and then runs runner registration on them again, which can disrupt a job already running on one.
  > On beta 2, restart only when no jobs are running. The fix shipped in [beta 3](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/blog/beta-3.md), and
  > [Restarts](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/blob/main/docs/scaling.md#restarts) explains how recovery works. Sorry for the confusion.
- "Reset everything" reports what it left behind, and `kinhin reset` exits 1 in that case.
- A large `images:` image is checked against its own size before a Tart clone, not the base VM's.
- A warm VM is recycled at once when its pool is turned off, instead of holding a slot for up to an hour.
- Commands that run a child process no longer lose the last lines of stderr under load.
- Video text wraps on whole words and shrinks to fit, so titles and captions stay inside the frame.
- The Capacity card's base-image rows fit their card again.

### What changed under the hood

- A repository's config now lives at `.kinhin/config.yml`. The older `.kinhin.yml` is still read when the new file is absent.
- Core toolchains (`node`, `go`, `python`, `ruby`, `swift`) install a pinned default when listed without a version, so a re-bake
  reproduces the same versions.
- The video image is pinned by digest, and Dependabot keeps it current.

## What has been run

Here is what this release has been through, in the terms I use everywhere in this post. **Run** means it was executed for
this release. **Not yet** means it has not been, and I am not claiming it.

- **Run:** the unit suite (3,377 tests, which need no VMs or network), the ThreadSanitizer run on the branch, the video
  suite's unit tests (81 of 81), and the release build's own check, which ran before signing.
- **Run:** the launch video was built from the same suite, with its size, loudness and caption checks passing.
- **Run:** the six healing scenarios on Gitea over Docker, through the end-to-end suite on 2026-10-14. The Tart warm-VM
  case has not run.
- **Not yet:** the end-to-end suite on this release, and its GitHub lane against a throwaway repository. The suite runs
  only in CI, and the CI runner for it is not registered yet.
- **Not yet:** upgrading from beta 1 on a Mac with real state.
- **Not yet:** the in-app updater has not been run against this release.

The beta-1 end-to-end results still stand for the forges as they were, but they have not been repeated on this release.

## Try it

The release is published on [GitHub](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/releases/tag/v0.0.1-beta-2). Install it with:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

You need an Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 15 or newer with about 60 GB of free disk, and an access token for your forge. The
[Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md) goes from install to a running fleet.

## Where I need help

I have one Mac and a finite supply of evenings. The most useful things to test are the ones I could not:

1. **The updater.** Install beta 1, let it find this release, and tell me whether it installed the update.
2. **Upgrading with real state.** Your fleet, project images and config, on beta 1, then beta 2. Tell me if anything was lost.
3. **The healing agent.** Run `kinhin heal` on a real fleet and send me any journal entry that looks wrong.
4. **Warm pools per image.** Route a job to an `images:` entry with `warm_pool` set, and tell me whether the VM was ready.
5. **Videos from your repo.** Make one with `kinhin video init` and `build`, and send me what you got.
6. **Real projects on the supported forges.** Your workflows, not my test jobs: GitHub, Gitea, Forgejo and GitLab CE.

One real job is a valuable report, including when it fails. Open a
[forge or runtime report](https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/issues/new/choose) and say what you ran and what went wrong.
Attach the output of `kinhin doctor --bundle` after a glance through it, since it is redacted but not perfect.

## Thank you

kinhin is free and Apache-2.0. If it saves you CI minutes, you can [support it](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/support.md).

# Alternatives to Orchard for CI on a Mac

Orchard and kinhin solve different problems, so the right alternative depends on what you need.

**Orchard** is a controller and workers that manage Tart VMs across a cluster of Apple Silicon Macs, with a CLI and a REST API.
It schedules VMs. It does not connect to a CI service, so you still need something that turns a queued CI job into a VM.

**kinhin** is that second part. It watches the queue of your CI service, decides how many runners the queue needs, and places
them on one Mac. It is a CI runner autoscaler, not a cluster.

## If you need CI runners on one Mac

- **kinhin:** queue-driven autoscaling for GitHub Actions, GitLab, Gitea and Forgejo, with a menu bar app and a daemon.
- **runscaler:** a command-line autoscaler for GitHub Actions. Pick it when you use only GitHub and want a small tool.
- **Cilicon and Tartelet:** macOS apps that run ephemeral Tart VMs as runners. Both are smaller in scope.
- **GitLab Runner with the Tart executor:** one VM per job, with concurrency set by hand in `config.toml`.

## If you need many Macs

kinhin manages the Mac it runs on and does not schedule across machines. For a fleet of Macs, an orchestrator is the better
foundation. Orchard is one. Commercial options are Anka Build and Orka, which both run VM fleets with central management.

The [comparison](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/compare.md) has the detail on each tool, with links to their documentation.

## Next steps

- [Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md): From zero to a working fleet
- [Install](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md): Pinned versions, updates and uninstall
- [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md): What has been run against a real server
- [Why kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md): Why most runners do one job at a time

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-many-macos-vms-can-run-at-once.md

# How many macOS VMs can run at once?

Two. Apple's licence and its Virtualization framework limit one Mac to two macOS guest VMs running at the same time. Linux
guests are not subject to that limit. The [why kinhin exists](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md) page has the sources.

So a design that runs one VM per runner tops out at two parallel macOS jobs on one Mac, however fast the Mac is.

## How kinhin gets past two

- **Several runners in one VM.** `runners_per_vm` runs more than one runner process inside a single Tart VM, so one VM can
  take several jobs. Size `vm.cpu` and `vm.memory_gb` for the sum of the jobs it will run. See
  [Job density](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/scaling.md#job-density).
- **Linux jobs in containers or Linux VMs.** Linux jobs run in apple/container microVMs, Docker containers, or Tart Linux VMs.
  The two-VM limit applies to macOS guests only. See [Runtimes](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/runtimes.md).

The cap still depends on your Mac. Cores, memory and free disk set how many jobs fit at once, as described in
[How scaling works](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/scaling.md#capacity).

## Next steps

- [Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md): From zero to a working fleet
- [Install](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md): Pinned versions, updates and uninstall
- [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md): What has been run against a real server
- [Why kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md): Why most runners do one job at a time

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-autoscale-github-actions-runners-on-a-mac.md

# How to autoscale GitHub Actions runners on a Mac

Autoscaling means the number of runners follows the queue. When jobs wait, kinhin starts more VMs. When the queue empties,
the VMs are deleted, so nothing idles between builds. You set the ceiling; kinhin works out how many runners the Mac can
actually hold.

Set up the first fleet with [How to run GitHub Actions on a self-hosted Mac](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-run-github-actions-on-a-self-hosted-mac.md).
This page covers how the fleet grows.

## How big the fleet gets

kinhin's concurrency cap is the smallest of these:

- `max_runners`, the ceiling you set
- your cores after `reserve.cpu`, divided by `vm.cpu`
- your memory after `reserve.memory_gb`, divided by `vm.memory_gb`
- your free disk, divided by the disk each VM needs

Before every spawn, kinhin checks free disk again. It holds new VMs when the disk would drop below `reserve.disk_gb` plus one
VM's footprint, so a burst of jobs cannot fill the disk. `kinhin doctor` prints the cap and which limit is binding.

## Keep VMs warm for faster starts

A cold job pays for a clone and a boot before it runs. Set `warm_pool` to keep booted, unregistered VMs ready, so the next
job skips both. The warm pool is off by default. It covers jobs that use the base image on Tart; jobs with a per-project
image still clone and boot. See [Warm pool](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/scaling.md#warm-pool).

## What autoscaling does not do

kinhin manages the one Mac it runs on. It does not schedule jobs across several Macs. If you have a rack of Macs, read
[the comparison](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/compare.md) before you choose a tool.

## Next steps

- [Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md): From zero to a working fleet
- [Install](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md): Pinned versions, updates and uninstall
- [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md): What has been run against a real server
- [Why kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md): Why most runners do one job at a time

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-generate-localized-app-store-screenshots.md

# How to generate localized app store screenshots

List the languages once. The screenshots lane runs your UI tests for each language and writes each set into its own folder.
The lane sets the language, but your app still has to show it: every language needs translated strings in the app, or each
locale shows the same text.

## Set the languages

- **iOS:** set `SNAPSHOT_LANGUAGES`, for example `en-US,fr-FR`, then run `bundle exec fastlane screenshots`.
- **Android:** set `SCREENGRAB_LOCALES` the same way.

```bash
SNAPSHOT_LANGUAGES=en-US,fr-FR bundle exec fastlane screenshots   # iOS
SCREENGRAB_LOCALES=en-US,fr-FR bundle exec fastlane screenshots   # Android
```

Each language gets its own folder, such as `fastlane/screenshots/fr-FR/` on iOS.

## Translate the strings

Add a translation for each language in the app itself. On iOS that is the string catalog or `Localizable.strings`. On Android
it is a `values-fr/strings.xml` folder next to `values/strings.xml`. Without these, the French screenshots show English text.

## What has been verified

In kinhin's own runs, both platforms captured `en-US` and `fr-FR` in one run, each in its own folder. Those runs used sample
apps that translate a single string, so the locale switch is visible, but the sample apps do not show a full translation.

The [Store screenshots](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-screenshots.md#locales) page covers the locale settings and the folder layout.

## Next steps

- [Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md): From zero to a working fleet
- [Install](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md): Pinned versions, updates and uninstall
- [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md): What has been run against a real server
- [Why kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md): Why most runners do one job at a time

# How to make a product launch video from code

Write the video as a config file in your repository: the scenes, a voice-over, music, captions and a theme. One command
renders it into an MP4, a WebM, a poster image, a GIF and a caption file. Because the video is built from the repo, the next
release can rebuild it instead of someone re-editing a timeline.

## Steps

1. **Create a starter video.** Run `kinhin video init launch` in your repository. It writes a starter config under
   `.kinhin/videos/`.
2. **Write the scenes.** Title, statement, stats, steps and code scenes are drawn, so they need no screen recording. The
   [video config reference](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-config.md) lists every scene and setting.
3. **Build it.** Run `kinhin video build launch`. Flags change the theme, format, captions and music for one build.
4. **Find the output.** It lands in `.kinhin/videos/out/launch/`: `launch.mp4`, `launch.webm`, `launch-poster.png`,
   `launch-hero.gif` and the caption file.

## What you need

- A container runtime. kinhin uses Apple's `container` if it is running, otherwise Docker.
- Disk space. The first build pulls a container image of about 1 GB.

No accounts are needed. To rebuild the video in CI on every release, see [Marketing video in CI](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/ci-video.md). That is
off by default and opt-in per repository.

For an example, see the [video gallery](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/video-gallery.md). Or read [Add videos to your project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md)
for the full walk-through.

## Next steps

- [Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md): From zero to a working fleet
- [Install](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md): Pinned versions, updates and uninstall
- [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md): What has been run against a real server
- [Why kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md): Why most runners do one job at a time

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-run-fastlane-screenshots-in-ci-on-a-mac.md

# How to run fastlane screenshots in CI on a Mac

Screenshot capture needs a Mac: iOS screenshots come from simulators, and Xcode runs only on macOS. kinhin provides that Mac
as a runner, and the workflow runs the `screenshots` lane on it. The VM is deleted when the job ends, so the workflow also
uploads the PNGs as an artifact. Without that step the screenshots disappear with the VM.

## Steps

1. **Set up the fleet.** Install kinhin and start the runner as in
   [How to run GitHub Actions on a self-hosted Mac](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-run-github-actions-on-a-self-hosted-mac.md).
2. **Add the screenshot settings.** Set the repository variables under **Settings**, then **Secrets and variables**, then
   **Variables**. `SNAPSHOT_LANGUAGES` sets the iOS languages and defaults to `en-US`.
3. **Run the lane by hand.** Start the mobile workflow and choose `screenshots` as the lane.
4. **Download the screenshots.** When the run finishes, open its page and download the `ios-screenshots` artifact. It is kept
   for 14 days.

The artifact is visible to everyone who can read the workflow run. Use test accounts and fake data on the screens the lane
captures.

## What has been verified

The iOS lane has been run locally on a simulator. The Android job needs an Android emulator on the runner, and the runner
image has to provide it. That setup has not been verified on a runner yet.

The [Store screenshots](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-screenshots.md) page has every workflow variable and the artifact details.

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-run-gitea-or-forgejo-actions-on-a-mac.md

# How to run Gitea or Forgejo Actions on a Mac

Gitea and Forgejo use the same runner, so kinhin sets them up the same way. Add a Gitea or Forgejo account to your config,
then send jobs to the Mac with a label. Each job gets a fresh VM, and kinhin deletes it after the runner goes idle.

## Set it up

Install kinhin and start the fleet as in
[How to run GitHub Actions on a self-hosted Mac](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-run-github-actions-on-a-self-hosted-mac.md). Then add the account:

```yaml
accounts:
  - name: gitea # or "forgejo" with forge: forgejo
    forge: gitea
    instance: "https://gitea.example.com"
    scope: "owner/name" # or an org name
    labels: ["macos:host"] # jobs opt in via runs-on: macos:host
```

The token is an access token with runner-management rights on the scope. Store it with `kinhin auth set --gitea` or
`kinhin auth set --forgejo`.

In the workflow, ask for the Mac by its label:

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos:host
```

## Minimum runners depend on the version

Gitea 1.24 and older report no queued job until a runner exists, so set `min_runners: 1` for them. Gitea 1.25 and later,
and Forgejo 11 and later, list queued jobs themselves and work with `min_runners: 0`.

kinhin has run end to end on Gitea 1.24 and 1.26 and on Forgejo 11. See the [tested-forge table](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md#what-has-been-tested).

The runner has no single-job mode, so kinhin deletes the VM shortly after its runners go idle.

## Next steps

- [Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md): From zero to a working fleet
- [Install](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md): Pinned versions, updates and uninstall
- [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md): What has been run against a real server
- [Why kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md): Why most runners do one job at a time

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-run-github-actions-on-a-self-hosted-mac.md

# How to run GitHub Actions on a self-hosted Mac

kinhin turns one Apple Silicon Mac into a fleet of self-hosted GitHub Actions runners. It watches your queue, starts a fresh
macOS VM for each queued job, registers a runner that takes one job, and deletes the VM when the job ends. Your workflow
changes by one line: `runs-on`.

## What you need

- An Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 15 or later, with about 60 GB of free disk. [Hardware and sizing](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/hardware.md) shows how
  much fleet a given Mac can run.
- A GitHub token for the repository or organization, with the permissions listed under [GitHub in Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md#github).

## Set it up

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/RabinApps/kinhin/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
kinhin setup repair tart
kinhin config init
kinhin auth set
kinhin image prepare && kinhin start
```

In `kinhin config init`, add a `github` account with your repository or organization as its `scope`. Then point a job at
the fleet:

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos, arm64]
```

Run `kinhin watch` to see jobs arrive and runners start.

## What happens to each job

1. The job is queued on GitHub, and kinhin sees it.
2. kinhin starts a linked-clone VM from the base image.
3. The VM registers one runner, which takes the job and no other.
4. When the job ends, the runner is removed and the VM is deleted. Nothing carries over to the next job.

How many jobs run at once depends on your Mac. kinhin caps the fleet from your cores, memory and free disk. See
[How scaling works](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/scaling.md#capacity).

## Before you point a public repository at it

A pull request from a fork can run code on your Mac. Read [Open-source projects](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/open-source.md) before you connect a
public repository.

## Status

GitHub Actions has been run by hand against github.com. Its end-to-end test lane is not run yet. The
[tested-forge table](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md#what-has-been-tested) has the current state.

## Next steps

- [Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md): From zero to a working fleet
- [Install](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md): Pinned versions, updates and uninstall
- [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md): What has been run against a real server
- [Why kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md): Why most runners do one job at a time

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-run-gitlab-ci-jobs-on-a-mac.md

# How to run GitLab CI jobs on a Mac

kinhin runs those jobs on an Apple Silicon Mac that you own. It watches your GitLab queue for tagged jobs and creates a runner
through the GitLab API for each job that is waiting. The runner takes one job, and the VM and the runner are deleted when
it ends.

## Set it up

Install kinhin, store its tokens and start the fleet as in
[How to run GitHub Actions on a self-hosted Mac](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-run-github-actions-on-a-self-hosted-mac.md). Then add a GitLab account
to `kinhin config`:

```yaml
accounts:
  - name: gitlab
    forge: gitlab
    scope: "group/project" # or a group path; subgroups nest
    instance: "https://gitlab.example.com"
    labels: ["macos"] # runner tags
```

The token needs the `create_runner`, `manage_runner` and `read_api` scopes, or `api`. Creating runners needs Maintainer on a
project or Owner on a group. Store the token with `kinhin auth set`.

Ask for the Mac in your `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
build:
  tags: [macos]
  script: xcodebuild -version
```

A waiting job counts as demand only when every tag it asks for is one that a pool advertises, so the tag must match the
`labels` you set.

## Good to know

- kinhin's GitLab support has been run end to end on GitLab CE 18.4. It supports self-managed GitLab CE 16.0 and later.
- Keep `vm.ephemeral` on. GitLab runners delete themselves after one job, so kinhin rejects `vm.ephemeral: false` for a
  GitLab account.
- Only tagged jobs in projects the token can read count. A project the token cannot read is an error, not an empty queue.

Full field reference: [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md#gitlab).

## Next steps

- [Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md): From zero to a working fleet
- [Install](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md): Pinned versions, updates and uninstall
- [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md): What has been run against a real server
- [Why kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md): Why most runners do one job at a time

# How to take App Store screenshots automatically

Take the screenshots from UI tests instead of a simulator you tap through by hand. A UI test opens each screen and saves a
screenshot at the point you choose. fastlane runs the tests, so the same screenshots come out again each time the app
changes. On iOS the tool is `snapshot`; on Android it is `screengrab`.

kinhin writes the wiring: a `screenshots` lane, the settings files and sample tests.

## Steps

1. **Add the lane.** Run `kinhin mobile init` in your project. It writes the settings, the sample tests and the lane. It does
   not edit your Xcode project or your Gradle files.
2. **Add a UI test target (iOS, once).** In Xcode, add a UI Testing Bundle target. The
   [iOS setup steps](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-screenshots.md#ios-set-up-the-ui-test-target) show each click.
3. **Write the tests.** Replace the sample tests with tests that open your screens. Call `snapshot("01-home")` on iOS or
   `Screengrab.screenshot("01-home")` on Android at each screen.
4. **Run the lane.** From the folder that holds `fastlane/`, run `bundle exec fastlane screenshots`. On iOS you get one PNG
   per `snapshot` call and language, in `fastlane/screenshots/`.

Framing with frameit is optional. Uploading to the stores is off until you turn it on.

## What has been verified

The iOS lane has been run on an iPhone 17e simulator, and the output layout above is what it wrote. Read
[Store screenshots with fastlane](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-screenshots.md) for every setting and the Android details.

For a full walk-through, including the first build, see [Tutorial: first build](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-fastlane-tutorial.md).

# Self-hosted alternative to GitHub-hosted macOS runners

kinhin runs GitHub Actions macOS jobs on an Apple Silicon Mac that you own. Like GitHub-hosted runners, each job gets a fresh
VM that is deleted when the job ends. The difference is where the Mac lives and who pays for it: kinhin is free and open
source under Apache-2.0, and the hardware, power and upkeep are yours.

## When kinhin fits

- You already have Apple Silicon Macs, or you are willing to buy one, and you run many macOS jobs. A busy Mac can cost less
  than per-minute macOS runner charges.
- You want jobs to run on your own network, with your own toolchains and caches. See [Toolchains](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/toolchains.md).
- You need several jobs at once. kinhin runs a fleet on one Mac; see [How scaling works](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/scaling.md).

## When GitHub-hosted runners fit better

- **You need Intel macOS.** kinhin needs an Apple Silicon Mac.
- **You do not want hardware.** Nothing to buy, power, update or repair.
- **Your jobs are rare.** A Mac that waits for work all day is wasted money.

## Other options

Several hosted macOS services exist, along with other self-hosted tools. The [comparison](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/compare.md) covers them with
what each does well.

To start, follow [How to run GitHub Actions on a self-hosted Mac](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/how-to-run-github-actions-on-a-self-hosted-mac.md).

## Next steps

- [Quick start](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/quick-start.md): From zero to a working fleet
- [Install](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/install.md): Pinned versions, updates and uninstall
- [Forge support](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/forges.md): What has been run against a real server
- [Why kinhin](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/why-kinhin.md): Why most runners do one job at a time

# Architecture: screenshots

How `kinhin mobile init` sets up store screenshots, what the lane does on each platform, and how the screenshots leave the
VM. This page is a companion to the [architecture overview](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/architecture.md); the setup guide is
[Store screenshots with fastlane](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-screenshots.md).

[← Back to architecture](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/architecture.md)

## Scope

Screenshots are a fastlane job, not a kinhin runtime. kinhin scaffolds the files and runs the workflow on a runner, and
fastlane does the capture, framing and upload. kinhin never edits your Xcode project or your Gradle files, because a
script that edits them is easy to break. Those steps are manual and documented in the setup guide.

## Scaffolding

`Sources/KinhinKit/Mobile/` holds the templates and scaffold logic. `kinhin mobile init` writes three kinds of file:

| Written by kinhin | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Lane | The project's `fastlane` folder (`screenshots` lane) | Calls `snapshot` on iOS or `screengrab` on Android |
| Settings | `fastlane/Snapfile`, `fastlane/Framefile.json`, `fastlane/Screengrabfile` | Devices, languages, frames, locales |
| Sample UI tests | `UITests/` (iOS), `app/src/androidTest/java/screenshots/` (Android) | The screens fastlane photographs |

You still add the UI test target to the Xcode project, and the instrumented test source set to Gradle.

## Capture on each platform

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    lane["fastlane screenshots"] --> ios["iOS: snapshot"]
    lane --> android["Android: screengrab"]
    ios --> sim["Simulator runs UI tests<br>one run per device and language"]
    android --> emu["Emulator or device runs instrumented tests<br>one run per locale"]
    sim --> png["PNGs per locale<br>fastlane/screenshots or metadata/android"]
    emu --> png
    png --> frame{"FRAME_SCREENSHOTS = 1?"}
    frame -- yes --> frameit["frameit adds device frames"]
    frame -- no --> out["Screenshot folders"]
    frameit --> out
    out --> up{"UPLOAD_SCREENSHOTS = 1?"}
    up -- yes --> store["Upload to App Store Connect or Google Play"]
    up -- no --> keep["Kept on disk"]
```

The lane exits 0 only when at least one PNG exists, so an empty run fails loudly rather than passing silently. Upload is
off unless you turn it on, and framing is optional.

Each platform's settings map to fastlane's own options. Variables set in the CI workflow choose the devices, languages,
locales and frame and upload toggles. The full list is in the [settings table](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/mobile-screenshots.md#settings-from-ci).

## CI flow

The CI job runs the lane on the macOS runner, then uploads the screenshots as a workflow artifact. The VM is deleted when
the job ends, so the artifact is the only copy that survives.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    job["mobile job on a macOS runner"] --> run["Run lane<br>iOS and Android"]
    run --> artifact["Upload artifact<br>ios-screenshots or android-screenshots, kept 14 days"]
    artifact --> reader["Anyone who can read the run"]
    run -. "upload toggle" .-> stores["App Store Connect or Google Play"]
```

Upload the artifact even when the lane fails, so the partial screenshots are available for debugging. Because anyone who
can read the run can open the artifact, the sample screens use test accounts and fake data.

The Android job runs on the same macOS runner as iOS. screengrab needs an emulator or device on that runner, which the
runner image must provide. The setup has not been verified on a runner.

## From screenshots to a video

Screenshots can feed a launch video. A `device` scene in a project's video file takes PNG paths as `props.screens` and shows
them as a cross-fading slideshow. The `mobile-capture` job in the video workflow captures them for a look that sets
`screens`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    shots["Screenshot PNGs"] --> scene["device scene<br>props.screens"]
    scene --> build["kinhin video build"]
    build --> video["Launch video"]
```

See [making a video](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/making-a-video.md#screenshots-as-a-scene) and [CI video](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/ci-video.md#store-screenshots-in-the-mobile-cut)
for the details.

---

Source: https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/architecture-videos.md

# Architecture: videos

How `kinhin video` turns a repository's video project into an MP4, and how the marketing video runs in CI. This page is
a companion to the [architecture overview](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/architecture.md); the product-facing guides are [Videos for your project](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/videos-for-your-project.md),
[Making kinhin's demo video](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/making-a-video.md) and [Marketing video in CI](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/ci-video.md).

[← Back to architecture](https://kinhin.dev/v0.0.1-beta-4/guide/architecture.md)

## The two halves

A video build has two halves that never share state beyond the output folder:

1. **Capture.** Adapters record the product (an app window, a terminal session, a browser session). Recording happens on
   the host or in a throwaway VM, and each clip is committed under the adapter folder.
2. **Render.** The build runs inside a container image, so a Linux runner can produce the same file as a Mac. It turns the
   project file, the clips and the narration into scenes, then assembles them.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    adapter["Adapter<br>video/adapters/name"] -- record-app, record-web, VHS tapes --> clips["Committed clips"]
    project["Project file<br>scenes, looks, captions"] -- scenes, looks, captions --> build
    clips --> build["kinhin video build<br>video/scripts/build.sh"]
    build -- "runs inside" --> image["Video image<br>Node, Motion Canvas, Chromium, ffmpeg"]
    image --> output["out/project/*.mp4, webm, poster, hero GIF, srt"]
    output --> verify["verify.mjs<br>frame size, length, loudness, blank frames"]
```

Only the render half needs the container runtime. The capture half needs a Mac for app clips, which is why app recordings
are committed rather than rebuilt in CI.

## Local build, step by step

`kinhin video build` plans the run, picks a runtime, makes sure the image exists, and then runs the steps below in the
container. The runner (`VideoRunner`) decides which runtime to use: `preferred` if given, else Apple's `container` when its
service is running, else Docker when its daemon answers. Missing images are pulled once; the first pull is about a
gigabyte.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    cli["kinhin video build"] --> plan["VideoRunner: plan<br>runtime, image, output folder"]
    plan --> pull["Pull or build image"]
    pull --> voice["voice.mjs: render narration cues"]
    voice --> retime["retime.mjs: fit each scene to its speech<br>timing.ts, timeline.json, captions.srt"]
    retime --> titles["render-titles.mjs: draw canvas scenes headlessly"]
    titles --> frames["frames.mjs: put device and terminal clips in frames"]
    frames --> music["fetch-music.mjs: checked music track"]
    music --> assemble["assemble.mjs: join scenes, fades, voice, ducked music, captions"]
    assemble --> out["out/project/project.mp4 and siblings"]
```

Three steps are cached under `.kinhin/videos/.cache` (the `raw/` folder of the build), each by a hash of everything that shapes
its result, so a second build after a one-line edit redoes only what that line touches: the voice of each sentence
(`voice-cache/`, `scripts/voice.mjs`), the drawn scenes (`scenes/`, `scripts/render-titles.mjs`) and the framed recordings
(`frames/`, `scripts/frames.mjs`: the clip's bytes, the scene's props and length, the look and the framing scripts). The
`out/.work/` folder is scratch and is removed by the container build. `build.sh` prints how long each step took and
`assemble.mjs` how long each part of the final cut did. `--scene` (`VIDEO_SCENES`) builds a subset of the scenes for a quick
preview, and `kinhin video build --watch` repeats the build when the repository's video files change.

## Scene types

A project is a list of scenes. Each scene is one of two kinds, and the pipeline does not know about any product:

| Kind | Drawn by | Source of the pixels |
|---|---|---|
| Canvas scene (title, statement, queue, parallel, map, outro) | Motion Canvas, rendered headlessly | The project file's text and theme |
| Clip scene (`device`, `terminal`, `browser`) | Clip framing in `frames.mjs` | A committed recording from the adapter |

Everything specific to one product lives in the adapter: `video/adapters/<name>/`, with its recorders, tape files, committed
clips and claims rules.

## Capture paths

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph app["App clip"]
        appRec["record-app.sh<br>kinhin video record on a Mac"] --> appClip["committed clip"]
        appTart["record-app-in-tart.sh<br>throwaway Tart VM"] --> appClip
    end
    subgraph web["Browser clip"]
        webRec["record-web.sh<br>Playwright in a container or locally"] --> webClip["committed clip"]
    end
    subgraph term["Terminal clip"]
        tape["VHS tape per variant"] --> termClip["committed clip"]
    end
```

Browser clips need no Mac, no desktop session and no permission grant, so they are the easiest path for anything that runs
in a browser. Terminal clips run the real CLI from a debug build in a throwaway support folder.

The demo app for kinhin's own video is a debug-only `FleetServing` (`Sources/kinhin-app/Demo/`) that replays a script. It
touches no config, Keychain, daemon or forge.

## Verification

`video/scripts/verify.mjs` is the same checker the end-to-end tests use. A video that fails it is not published. It checks:

- the frame size and the length against the timeline,
- an audio track near -16 LUFS,
- no black frames,
- one caption per cue,
- a poster and a hero GIF that are not blank,
- the size and length budgets.

`kinhin video validate` checks the project and its claims without rendering, so a bad claim fails fast.

## CI

The marketing video runs as a GitHub Actions workflow. Publishing is the only part that touches the release or the site.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    plan["plan<br>decide what to build"] --> claims["claims<br>reject unsupported claims"]
    claims --> build["build, one job per look<br>build.sh --container, then verify"]
    build --> publishRelease["publish-release<br>reviewed, marketing environment"]
    build --> publishSite["publish-site<br>site pull request, reviewed"]
```

- **plan** works out which looks to build, in seconds.
- **claims** is the honesty gate. It reads `video/adapters/<name>/claims.json` and the project file, and it fails a video
  that says something the product does not support.
- **build** pulls the image published for the release (`ghcr.io/rabinapps/kinhin-video:<version>`) when there is one, and
  builds it from the checked-out sources otherwise. It then runs the same checks as `verify.mjs` and writes a summary.
- **publish** steps run only after a build succeeds, and only behind the `marketing` environment, so a person approves them.

A failed video job never blocks a release, a docs deploy or a pull request, because nothing depends on it.
